## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/preference/bradley_terry.py:209-218`, `next_pair()` calculates the score gap between candidates using `gap = abs(strengths.get(a, 1.0) - strengths.get(b, 1.0)) if strengths else 0.0`. When `strengths` mapping contains explicit `None` values (such as from un-fitted items or failed model estimations), `strengths.get(a, 1.0)` evaluates to `None`, triggering `TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for -: 'NoneType' and 'float'`. In addition, if `strengths` contains non-finite floats (`math.nan`), `gap` evaluates to `nan`, causing `gap < best[0]` to evaluate to `False` and silently dropping the pair.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/preference/bradley_terry.py`
- `tests/test_bradley_terry.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: catching `TypeError` inside the outer loop and skipping pair comparisons without sanitizing node strengths is a failure of this issue.
- Do not alter the component graph connection logic in Rule 1 of `next_pair()`.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add numeric sanitization in `next_pair()` in `src/fine_art_archive/preference/bradley_terry.py` to default `None` and non-finite strengths to `1.0`.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_bradley_terry.py` verifying `next_pair()` handles `None` and `NaN` values in `strengths` without raising TypeError or dropping valid pairs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_bradley_terry.py` passes cleanly.
- Calling `next_pair(["work-a", "work-b"], [], strengths={"work-a": None, "work-b": 1.0})` returns `("work-a", "work-b")` without raising TypeError.
- Deliberate break: remove `None` check in `src/fine_art_archive/preference/bradley_terry.py`, run `pytest tests/test_bradley_terry.py`, and verify the None-strength test fails; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Define a small helper `_get_finite_strength(strengths, key, default=1.0)` in `src/fine_art_archive/preference/bradley_terry.py`.
title: [P2] Guard None and non-finite values in Bradley-Terry next_pair selection

body:
## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/parsers/dimension_utils.py:25-78`, `parse_dimension_pair()` matches dimension pairs using regular expression `DIMENSION_PAIR_TOKEN` and selects unit via `unit = (second_unit or first_unit or "cm").lower()`. When given 3D physical dimension strings with a trailing unit such as `"535 x 463 x 52 mm"`, the regex captures the first two numbers (`535` and `463`) with empty unit groups because `"mm"` is attached to the third number (`52 mm`). The function defaults to `"cm"`, parsing the dimension as `(463.0, 535.0)` cm instead of `(46.3, 53.5)` cm. This 10x error causes `dim_compat("53.5 x 46.3 cm", "535 x 463 x 52 mm")` to report `"mismatch"` (relative difference 0.90), failing duplicate detection for 3D or framed museum objects.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/parsers/dimension_utils.py`
- `tests/test_dimension_utils.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: returning hardcoded conversions for mm without handling 3D depth dimensions (`H x W x D`) in regex matching is a failure of this issue.
- Do not change the 5% relative tolerance threshold in `dim_compat()`.

## Tasks
- [ ] Update `DIMENSION_PAIR_TOKEN` and parsing in `src/fine_art_archive/parsers/dimension_utils.py` to recognize optional depth dimensions (`x <depth> <unit>`) and capture trailing units.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_dimension_utils.py` verifying 3D dimension strings with trailing mm, cm, and in units convert to cm correctly and match 2D equivalent dimensions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_dimension_utils.py` passes cleanly.
- `parse_dimension_pair("535 x 463 x 52 mm")` returns `(46.3, 53.5)` in cm.
- `dim_compat("53.5 x 46.3 cm", "535 x 463 x 52 mm")[0]` returns `"match"`.
- Deliberate break: revert regex in `src/fine_art_archive/parsers/dimension_utils.py`, run `pytest tests/test_dimension_utils.py`, and verify the 3D unit test fails; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Allow optional `(?:\s*[×x]\s*\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?\s*(cm|mm|m|in|inch|inches)?)?` in `src/fine_art_archive/parsers/dimension_utils.py` and inspect all matched unit groups.
title: [P2] Parse 3D dimension strings with trailing units in physical dimension comparison

body:
## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py:264-277`, `_record_blended_stats()` computes source age during warmup using `age_days = (datetime.now(UTC) - first).total_seconds() / 86400.0`. It parses `first_seen` with `first = datetime.fromisoformat(str(first_seen).replace("Z", "+00:00"))`. When `first_seen` is an offset-naive ISO timestamp string (e.g. `"2026-08-01T12:00:00"`), `first` has `tzinfo=None`. Subtracting `first` from timezone-aware `datetime.now(UTC)` raises `TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`, which is not caught by `except ValueError:` and crashes `score_for()` and the entire acquisition assessment flow.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py`
- `tests/test_source_quality_wiring.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: silencing `TypeError` without ensuring parsed `first_seen` timestamps are coerced to timezone-aware UTC datetimes is a failure of this issue.
- Do not change the 30-day warmup blending formula or tier prior defaults.

## Tasks
- [ ] Coerce parsed `first` datetimes with `if first.tzinfo is None: first = first.replace(tzinfo=UTC)` and catch `(ValueError, TypeError)` in `src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py`.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_source_quality_wiring.py` verifying `score_for()` computes blended scores correctly when `first_seen` contains offset-naive ISO strings.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_source_quality_wiring.py` passes cleanly.
- Calling `score_for("cleveland", "western-painting-19c", aggregates=...)` with `first_seen="2026-08-01T12:00:00"` returns a valid finite float score without raising TypeError.
- Deliberate break: remove timezone coercion in `src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py`, run `pytest tests/test_source_quality_wiring.py`, and verify the naive timestamp test fails with TypeError; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Ensure both `Z` replacements and naive ISO strings are normalized to timezone-aware UTC in `src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py`.
title: [P1] Handle offset-naive timestamps in source-quality warmup blending

## Why
In `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py:291-298` and `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py:351-358`, `allocate()` and `allocate_monthly()` normalize custom budget shares across available lenses using `weights = {n: float(shares.get(n, 0.0)) for n in available}` and `total = sum(weights.values())`. When `shares` contains non-finite floats (`math.nan`, `math.inf`) or non-positive weights, `total` evaluates to `nan` (which fails `total <= 0`). `exact` calculates `nan` values, and converting to integer (`out = {n: int(v) for n, v in exact.items()}`) crashes with `ValueError: cannot convert float NaN to integer`. Non-positive or infinite weights can also produce negative slot allocations.

## Scope
- `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py`
- `tests/test_selection_lenses.py`

## Non-Goals
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: catching `ValueError` at call sites or returning empty dictionaries on invalid weights without validating each share against positive finite bounds is a failure of this issue.
- Do not redesign the round-robin candidate distribution loop or saturation caps.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add finite positive validation for shares in `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py` falling back to default shares or equal positive distribution when weights are non-finite or non-positive.
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_selection_lenses.py` asserting `allocate()` and `allocate_monthly()` safely handle NaN, infinity, and negative shares without raising ValueError.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `pytest tests/test_selection_lenses.py` passes with 100% success.
- Passing `shares={"canon": float("nan"), "atypicality": 1.0}` to `allocate(10, ["canon", "atypicality"], shares)` and `allocate_monthly(10, ["canon", "atypicality"], shares, monthly_cap=100, spent={})` produces valid non-negative integer allocations summing to the batch cap without crashing.
- Deliberate break: remove finite validation in `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py`, run `pytest tests/test_selection_lenses.py`, and verify that the NaN allocation tests fail; revert to pass.

## Implementation Notes
- Use `math.isfinite(w) and w > 0.0` when sanitizing shares in `src/fine_art_archive/selection/lenses.py`.
title: [P1] Reject non-finite and non-positive shares in lens allocation algorithms

## Why

This is a latent current break: `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:443-455` returns a `master.*` candidate after `exists()` without resolving and checking it, while `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:711-743` opens that result for preview and `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:794-805` supplies it to export. ## Why

This is a current break: `scripts/finalize_acquisition.py:136` records `source_quality_inputs`, `src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py:445` defines aggregation, and `src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py:544` writes the routing YAML, but no in-scope production entry point calls either aggregation function. `config/source_quality.yaml:2` is still generated on 2026-05-24, while `src/fine_art_archive/collect/acquisition_flow.py:235-236` consumes that configuration only when an external caller invokes the library routine.

## Scope

Provide an explicit repository-owned command to rebuild source-quality routing data from a supplied canonical works directory, and expose an assessment command that exercises configured source routing without embedding a machine-specific archive path.

## Implementation Notes

body:
> Follow-up discovered while implementing #598, and measured there. Not a defect in #598's change — a
> precondition #598 deliberately did not build, recorded so it is not lost.

## Why

`select_quality_diverse` requires a quality score **and** an embedding for every candidate work.
`src/fine_art_archive/preference/exhibition.py:73-74` refuses the whole selection otherwise:

```python
if work_id not in quality_scores or work_id not in embeddings:
    raise MissingEvidenceError(f"{work_id}: quality and embedding evidence are required")
```

Both must be supplied **by the caller**. `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:351-352` declares them as
request fields defaulting to empty:

```python
quality_scores: dict[str, float] = Field(default_factory=dict)
embeddings: dict[str, list[float]] = Field(default_factory=dict)
```

and `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:418-419` forwards them straight through. **Nothing in this
repository produces either.** Repo-wide, `embeddings` appears only in
`src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py`, `src/fine_art_archive/preference/exhibition.py` and
`src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py`, and in all three it is a parameter being passed along, never a
value being computed or read from disk. The only callers that supply it are tests, which build the
vectors inline.

The operator UI posts `{ spec, target, sample }` and carries no evidence. Measured 2026-08-25 against
the exact body the browser sends, with `selection_mode: "preference-diverse"`:

```
status: 400
{"detail": "near-a: quality and embedding evidence are required"}
```

So the mode is now requestable from the builder (#598) and cannot yet return a selection there. The
preview pane surfaces `detail`, so the operator sees that sentence rather than silence — the failure
is legible, not silent, which is why this is a follow-up and not a regression.

Note the asymmetry that makes this worth its own issue: `min_quality`
(`src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py:132`) reads the quality axis of the ratings log, which the
server already loads. So the quality half has an obvious in-repo source and the embedding half has
none at all. Solving one is not solving the other.

## Scope

- `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py` — derive the evidence server-side when the request omits it
- `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py` — pass what it derives; no change to the gate or the default
- `tests/test_eink_pipeline.py` — assert a UI-shaped request with no evidence returns a selection

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** alter `select_quality_diverse` or `_validate_inputs` in `src/fine_art_archive/preference/exhibition.py`. The requirement that evidence exist is correct; this issue supplies it.
- Do **not** change the default `selection_mode` from `"ordered"` in `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py`.
- Do **not** remove the `quality_scores` / `embeddings` request fields. A caller that supplies evidence must keep overriding whatever the server derives.
- Do **not** add a network call or a model download to the request path. Whatever produces embeddings must be precomputed or local.
- Do **not** add a human approval, review or check-in step anywhere in this path.
- **Scaffold is forbidden.** Random vectors, a constant embedding for every work, or an embedding that does not distinguish two visually different works does **NOT count as done** — a degenerate embedding makes the diversity term meaningless while appearing to work, which is worse than the 400. Shipping the derivation without the distinctness assertion is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Decide and document in `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py` where embeddings come from, and read them from that source when the request omits them
- [ ] Derive `quality_scores` from the ratings quality axis already loaded at `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:411` when the request omits them
- [ ] Keep request-supplied evidence authoritative over anything derived, in `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py`
- [ ] Return a clear 400 in `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py` naming the missing source when no embedding is available for a candidate, rather than a per-work message that reads like a client error
- [ ] Add `test_ui_shaped_request_without_evidence_returns_a_selection` to `tests/test_eink_pipeline.py`
- [ ] Assert in `tests/test_eink_pipeline.py` that two visually distinct fixture works receive different embeddings, so a degenerate producer fails

## Acceptance Criteria

**Named test gate:**
`pytest tests/test_eink_pipeline.py::test_ui_shaped_request_without_evidence_returns_a_selection`

1. The test posts to `/eink/playlist/preview` a body containing only `spec`, `target` and `sample` —
   the exact shape `einkPreview()` sends — with `selection_mode: "preference-diverse"` and a `limit`,
   and asserts the response is 200 with a non-empty `selection_diagnostics`.
2. Against the tree before the change that request returns **400**
   `"<work_id>: quality and embedding evidence are required"`. Verified 2026-08-25.
3. A companion assertion in the same test asserts that two fixture works with different visual
   content receive different derived embeddings, so a constant or random producer fails the gate.
4. **Deliberate-break demonstration:** after the change, make the derived embedding constant for
   every work, run the named node id, and quote the failure; then revert and quote the pass.
5. `python3 -m pytest tests/test_eink_pipeline.py tests/test_exhibition_selection.py` reports no new
   failures.
title: preference-diverse selection has no evidence producer, so the UI mode it now offers cannot return a selection

body:
> Audit provenance: 2026-08-23 F4 — body staged 2026-08-23 in `Code/Audits/Fine-Art-Archive/2026-08-23-issue-bodies/04-exhibition-selector-unreachable-from-the-ui.md`.

## Why

#549 added deterministic quality-times-diversity selection for bounded exhibitions
(`src/fine_art_archive/preference/exhibition.py`, `select_quality_diverse`). It answers the
question the e-paper builder exists to ask: which works go on the panel. It runs only when the
playlist spec carries `selection_mode == "preference-diverse"`
(`src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py:416`), and the default is `"ordered"`
(`src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py:134`).

The operator UI never sets it. `src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html:2086-2102` is `einkSpec()`, the
single place the browser builds a playlist spec, and it assembles ten keys — `sort`, `artists`,
`periods`, `all_tags`, `moods`, `min_fit`, `limit`, `exclude_filters`, `require_dossier` — and no
`selection_mode`. There is no control that emits it, in `src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html` or
`src/fine_art_archive/ui/dossier.html`.

So every playlist the operator previews, saves or exports through
`/eink/playlist/preview`, `/eink/playlist/export` and `/eink/playlists` uses `"ordered"`. The
selector's only execution path in the tree is `tests/test_eink_pipeline.py:277` and `:310`, which
construct the spec by hand.

The consequence is not only the selection. `select_quality_diverse` returns
`SelectionDiagnostic` records explaining why each work was chosen, which
`src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py:431` marshals into `PlaylistResult.selection_diagnostics`.
That field is computed, returned by the API, and rendered by nothing: `selection_diagnostics` does
not appear in `src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html`. The explanation of the choice is produced and
discarded on the one screen where the choice is made.

This is the 2026-08-08 audit's dominant defect class — a producer and a consumer that both work and
were never connected — recurring in code merged after that audit. Note the contrast in the same
subsystem: #548's `choose_render_strategy` was wired end to end on arrival
(`src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:445`, `:590`, `src/fine_art_archive/display/render.py:247`,
`:282`), so this is a gap in one feature's delivery, not a systemic wiring failure.

Confirmed by an adversarial reviewer on 2026-08-23 (codex, confidence 0.99), which located
`einkSpec()` independently.

## Scope

- `src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html` — add a selection-mode control to the e-paper builder and send it in the spec
- `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py` — no behaviour change; the gate and default stay as they are
- `tests/test_eink_pipeline.py` — assert the UI-shaped spec reaches the selector

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** change the default from `"ordered"` to `"preference-diverse"`. The default must stay `"ordered"` so existing saved playlists keep their ordering; this issue makes the other mode reachable, not automatic.
- Do **not** alter the selection algorithm in `src/fine_art_archive/preference/exhibition.py`.
- Do **not** remove the `limit`-required guard at `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py:419`. `preference-diverse` needs a limit; the UI must disable or validate the control when no limit is set rather than the backend silently coping.
- Do **not** add a human approval step, and do **not** introduce a second playlist spec builder alongside `einkSpec()`.
- **Scaffold is forbidden.** A hidden input, a commented-out control, a constant that is never read, or a control that sends the key but whose value never reaches `select_quality_diverse` does **NOT count as done**. Shipping the control without surfacing the diagnostics is a partial failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a selection-mode control to the e-paper builder markup in `src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html` with the two values `ordered` and `preference-diverse`
- [ ] Emit `spec.selection_mode` from `einkSpec()` in `src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html` only when the control is set to `preference-diverse`
- [ ] Prevent submitting `preference-diverse` without a limit in `src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html`, matching the guard at `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py:419`
- [ ] Render the returned `selection_diagnostics` in the preview output area of `src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html` so the reason each work was chosen is visible
- [ ] Add `test_ui_shaped_spec_reaches_preference_diverse_selection` to `tests/test_eink_pipeline.py` posting the exact key set `einkSpec()` produces
- [ ] Assert in `tests/test_eink_pipeline.py` that the response `selection_diagnostics` list is non-empty for that spec

## Acceptance Criteria

**Named test gate:**
`pytest tests/test_eink_pipeline.py::test_ui_shaped_spec_reaches_preference_diverse_selection`

1. The test posts to `/eink/playlist/preview` a spec containing exactly the keys `einkSpec()`
   produces at `src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html:2086-2102` **plus** `selection_mode` and `limit`,
   and asserts the response `selection_diagnostics` is non-empty.
2. A companion assertion in the same test posts the same spec **without** `selection_mode` and
   asserts `selection_diagnostics` is empty, pinning the default as `"ordered"`.
3. A grep-backed assertion that `selection_mode` appears in `src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html`.
   Against `6b45762` that substring is absent — verified 2026-08-23 — so the assertion fails today.
4. **Deliberate-break demonstration:** after the change, remove the `spec.selection_mode` assignment
   from `einkSpec()` in `src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html`, run the named node id, and quote the
   failure; restore it and quote the pass.
5. `python3 -m pytest tests/test_eink_pipeline.py tests/test_exhibition_selection.py` reports no new
   failures, and a manual smoke of the builder shows the diagnostics text in the preview pane.
title: The quality-diversity exhibition selector cannot be requested from any operator screen

> Audit provenance: 2026-08-23 F2 (observed, rendered evidence) — body staged 2026-08-23 in `Code/Audits/Fine-Art-Archive/2026-08-23-issue-bodies/02-weekly-review-page-renders-unmeasured-claims.md`.

## Why

`scripts/render_weekly_review.py` builds the page the owner uses to make decisions. Its own header,
emitted at `scripts/render_weekly_review.py:564`, makes an explicit provenance guarantee:

> "Every number below was measured on your Mac, not in the sandbox."

Four blocks of the same page violate it. Observed in rendered output on 2026-08-23 — the page was
generated from a payload, served on `127.0.0.1`, and read back through the accessibility tree
(`frontend_verify.py`, 4/4 assertions pass, `snapshotNodeCount: 257`; screenshots and aria snapshot
in `Code/Audits/Fine-Art-Archive/2026-08-23-assets/`).

**1. Every non-G41 grant is labelled with G47's scope, verbatim.**
`scripts/render_weekly_review.py:163-165` is a binary `if grant == "G41" ... else`, so any third
grant id inherits the G47 string. Rendered, from a payload containing grants G41, G47 and G99:

```
heading "G41 — 1 promotions (recorded scope: 8 duplicate pairs; metadata transfer + quarantine)"
heading "G47 — 1 promotions (recorded scope: 6 sidecars with wrong artist Q-IDs; modify-in-place only)"
heading "G99 — 1 promotions (recorded scope: 6 sidecars with wrong artist Q-IDs; modify-in-place only)"
```

The page asserts a "recorded scope" for an authorization it has never seen. This is the highest-cost
of the four: the surrounding paragraph tells the owner that "`operations.log` plus the authorizing
grant is the undo script", so a fabricated scope is a fabricated undo plan.

**2. A hardcoded count presented as a measurement.**
`scripts/render_weekly_review.py:279` emits "A further 78 staging directories duplicate works
already in the archive and are safe to clear on any verdict here." The 78 is a literal; nothing in
the payload produces it. Confirmed present in the rendered page.

**3. A hardcoded dated measurement.**
`scripts/render_weekly_review.py:329` emits "On 2026-08-01, 26 of 34 proposed quarantines were
display copies." Also a literal, also rendered.

**4. Four closed issues rendered as open and tracked.**
`scripts/render_weekly_review.py:336-352` hardcodes a table under the heading "The four completeness
issues — filed, no decision needed today", with the body text "These are on GitHub with full
evidence. Listed so you know what is tracked". All four are CLOSED on the remote, checked
2026-08-23: #406 closed 2026-08-08, #407 closed 2026-08-08, #409 closed 2026-08-08, #408 closed
2026-08-15. The renderer merged on 2026-08-18, after all four closures.

Row 408 is the worst shape, because it mixes provenance: the count is interpolated live from
`coll['qids_on_multiple']` while the status cell is the frozen string "= current collision
evidence". A live number beside a frozen status reads as measured, so the staleness is
undetectable from the page.

The file already contains the correct guard against exactly this. `evidence_title()` at
`scripts/render_weekly_review.py:36-52` refuses a heading whose numerals are not supplied
measurements, and its docstring names the motive: "prevents a copied count from surviving after the
payload changes (the historical 138-vs-88 failure)". It is applied at `:377`, `:396`, `:417`, `:436`
and `:470` — the five decision-card titles — and at none of the four blocks above.

Confirmed by two adversarial reviewers on 2026-08-23 (cursor, confidence 0.95; codex, 0.99).

## Scope

- `scripts/render_weekly_review.py` — derive the grant scope from the payload, remove the three frozen prose measurements, and make the filed-issues block payload-driven
- `tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py` — add rendering assertions that execute the module

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** redesign the page layout, styling, or the decision-card structure.
- Do **not** add a network call to the GitHub API from the renderer. The filed-issues block must come from the payload, so the page stays runnable offline and reproducible from its input.
- Do **not** delete the filed-issues block outright if the payload can carry it — the owner uses it for orientation. Removing it is acceptable only if no payload key exists for it.
- Do **not** add a human approval step, and do **not** widen `evidence_title()` into a linter over the whole file.
- **Scaffold is forbidden.** A `TODO`, a comment marking the literals as suspect, or a docstring note does **NOT count as done**. Leaving any of the four literals reachable in rendered output is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace the `if grant == "G41"` binary at `scripts/render_weekly_review.py:163-165` with a lookup from a payload-supplied grant-scope mapping
- [ ] Make an unknown grant id render an explicit "scope not recorded" string rather than another grant's scope in `scripts/render_weekly_review.py`
- [ ] Remove the hardcoded 78 at `scripts/render_weekly_review.py:279` and derive that count from the payload or drop the sentence
- [ ] Remove the hardcoded "26 of 34 proposed quarantines" dated claim at `scripts/render_weekly_review.py:329`
- [ ] Drive the filed-issues table at `scripts/render_weekly_review.py:336-352` from a payload key, including each issue's state, instead of four literal rows
- [ ] Route the grant `<h4>` heading in `scripts/render_weekly_review.py` through `evidence_title()` so its numerals must be supplied measurements
- [ ] Add `test_unknown_grant_does_not_inherit_another_grants_scope` to `tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py` that imports the module and renders a three-grant payload

## Acceptance Criteria

**Named test gate:**
`pytest tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py::test_unknown_grant_does_not_inherit_another_grants_scope`

1. The test imports `scripts/render_weekly_review.py` (via `importlib` on the script path) and
   renders a payload whose `ungranted.by_grant` contains `G41`, `G47` and one unknown id.
2. It asserts the unknown grant's rendered heading does **not** contain the substring
   `6 sidecars with wrong artist Q-IDs`. Against `6b45762` this assertion **fails** — verified
   2026-08-23 by rendering a G41/G47/G99 payload, where G99 rendered that exact string.
3. It asserts the rendered document contains neither `A further 78 staging directories` nor
   `26 of 34 proposed quarantines`. Both are present in today's rendered output.
4. It asserts every issue number in the filed-issues block appears in the payload it was given.
5. **Deliberate-break demonstration:** after the fix, restore the `else` branch at
   `scripts/render_weekly_review.py:163-165` so an unknown grant again falls through to the G47
   string, run the named node id, and quote the failure; then revert and quote the pass. Do the same
   for one of the two frozen literals.
6. `python3 -m pytest tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py` reports no failures after the change,
   and the render command `python3 scripts/render_weekly_review.py --date <date>` still writes an
   HTML file for a valid payload.
title: The weekly decision page renders frozen prose and four closed issues as measured fact

body:
> Audit provenance: 2026-08-23 F3 (machine-verified hollow gate) — body staged 2026-08-23 in `Code/Audits/Fine-Art-Archive/2026-08-23-issue-bodies/03-weekly-review-guard-test-executes-none-of-what-it-guards.md`.

## Why

`tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py` is titled "Regression tests for weekly review dated vs
served thumbnail paths (issue #561)". It runs zero lines of `scripts/render_weekly_review.py` or
`scripts/make_review_thumbs.py`.

Two of its three tests assert Python string operations on literals defined inside their own bodies.
`tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py:8-13` builds a one-entry dict and then asserts the value it
just inserted; `:16-20` calls `str.replace` on a literal and asserts the result. Neither imports
anything from the repository. The third, `:23-28`, asserts the two script files exist and that
`render_weekly_review.py` contains the substrings `_ACTIVE_REL` and `thumbs_{d}/`.

No test anywhere imports or executes either script — the only mentions in `tests/` are the three
file-path assertions in this same file.

**Verified two independent ways on 2026-08-23, against `6b45762`:**

Manual break. `scripts/render_weekly_review.py:60` is the line #561 fixed:

```python
src = _ACTIVE_REL.get(path) or furl(path)
```

Reintroducing the exact defect it repaired — `src = furl(path)`, which emits `file://` URLs that do
not load when the page is served over http, the failure #561 was opened for — leaves the suite at
**3 passed**. Only renaming the identifier so the substring vanishes produces a failure, and it
fails on `assert '_ACTIVE_REL' in <file text>`: a grep, not a behaviour.

Independent tool. `local_verify.py --base-ref cc68a88~1`, the deliberate-break verifier, run against
the tree immediately before #561 — a tree that contains **neither script** — returns
`1 failed, 2 passed`. Two of the three tests pass in a repository that does not contain the code
they are named after.

Because `scripts/render_weekly_review.py` is 663 lines that generate the owner's decision surface,
and because the sibling finding in this audit is four blocks of that file rendering unmeasured
claims, the absence of any executing test is what let those blocks ship. A test file that cannot
fail for the reason it was written is indistinguishable from no test, and it is worse than no test
because it reports coverage of a fix it does not observe.

## Scope

- `tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py` — replace the two tautologies with tests that execute the renderer
- `scripts/render_weekly_review.py` — no behaviour change required by this issue; a small payload fixture may be added under `tests/`

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** change any rendering behaviour in `scripts/render_weekly_review.py` under this issue. Behaviour changes belong to the sibling issue about unmeasured claims.
- Do **not** delete `tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py::test_weekly_review_scripts_exist_in_repo`. A file-existence check is cheap and catches accidental deletion; it is simply not a behaviour test.
- Do **not** commit a large real payload. The fixture must be a minimal synthetic dict, small enough to read in one screen.
- Do **not** raise or lower the project coverage floor to make this pass.
- **Scaffold is forbidden.** A renamed test, a `pytest.mark.skip`, an added docstring, or a test that imports the module without asserting on its output does **NOT count as done**. A test file that still passes against `cc68a88~1` is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a minimal synthetic weekly-review payload fixture to `tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py` covering the six required top-level keys the renderer reads
- [ ] Load `scripts/render_weekly_review.py` by path with `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` in `tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py` since `scripts/` is not an importable package
- [ ] Replace `test_dated_rel_uses_date_scoped_directory` in `tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py` with a test that calls the module's `thumb()` and asserts the emitted `src` attribute
- [ ] Replace `test_served_copy_rewrites_dated_thumb_prefix` in `tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py` with a test that populates `_ACTIVE_REL` and asserts the served relative path wins over the `file://` form
- [ ] Assert in `tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py` that a path absent from `_ACTIVE_REL` still falls back to the `file://` form, so the fix is pinned in both directions
- [ ] Record in `tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py` a module docstring line stating the tests execute the renderer rather than asserting on its source text

## Acceptance Criteria

**Named test gate:**
`pytest tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py::test_served_relative_path_wins_over_file_url`

1. The named node id executes `thumb()` from `scripts/render_weekly_review.py` and asserts the
   emitted `src` is the `thumbs_<date>/<name>` relative form when `_ACTIVE_REL` holds that path.
2. **Deliberate-break demonstration, already performed for the current test and to be repeated for
   the new one:** change `scripts/render_weekly_review.py:60` to `src = furl(path)` and run the
   named node id — it must fail. Then revert and re-run — it must pass. Quote both outputs in the
   PR. Verified 2026-08-23 that today's suite stays at `3 passed` through that same break, which is
   the defect being fixed.
3. `local_verify.py --worktree <checkout> --base-ref cc68a88~1 --test-path tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py --test-cmd 'python3 -m pytest tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py'`
   must report every test in the file failing against that base, not `1 failed, 2 passed` as it does
   today. A test that passes on a tree without the code is the condition being removed.
4. `python3 -m pytest tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py` passes on the current tip after the
   change, with at least one assertion per test referencing a value returned by the renderer.
5. Coverage of `scripts/render_weekly_review.py` under
   `python3 -m pytest tests/test_weekly_review_thumb_paths.py --cov=scripts` is above zero. It is
   0.00% today.
title: The #561 regression test executes no line of the two scripts it is named for

body:
> Audit provenance: 2026-08-23 F1 (successor to 2026-08-08 finding 37 / issue draft 01a) — body staged 2026-08-23 in `Code/Audits/Fine-Art-Archive/2026-08-23-issue-bodies/01-healthz-calls-zero-manifest-healthy.md`.

## Why

`manifest.csv` is the Companion App's only navigation path. The drift check added in #505
(`src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:196-200`) closed the 2026-08-05 gap where 18 promoted works were
servable but unfindable. It shipped with an escape hatch that admits the **worse** state.

The guard at `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:200`:

```python
drift_is_healthy = manifest_loaded == 0 or manifest_drift == 0
```

`manifest_loaded == 0` short-circuits without consulting `sidecar_works`, which is computed four
lines earlier in the same function. Measured live on a scratch clone of `6b45762` with the app
booted under `~/.faa-venv`:

| `sidecar_works` | `manifest_loaded` | `manifest_drift` | `ok` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3411 | 0 | -3411 | **`true`** |
| 3411 | 1 | -3410 | `false` |

The endpoint is more alarmed by losing 3,410 of 3,411 navigable works than by losing all 3,411. The
response is non-monotonic in the severity of the condition it exists to detect, and the total-loss
case is the one that reports healthy — it fails toward silence.

The allowance is deliberate, and its own stated rationale is narrower than its implementation.
`src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:196-199` says drift gates health "once a manifest exists and
claims content", and `tests/test_healthz_manifest_drift.py:76-93` pins the behaviour with a fixture
of exactly **one** sidecar — the fresh-checkout case named in that test's docstring ("A fresh
checkout ships a fixture sidecar and no manifest"). Nothing in either rationale covers 3,411
sidecars with no manifest, and no test exercises it.

The same file proves the authors reasoned about this exact hazard for the other operand:
`tests/test_healthz_manifest_drift.py:95-111` asserts an unreadable tree yields `None`, not `0`,
because "Reporting 0 there would make drift arithmetic read healthy in exactly the case health
should fire." That reasoning was applied to `sidecar_works` and not to `manifest_loaded`.

This is not a hypothetical state, it is the default one. **Nothing in this repository writes
`manifest.csv`.** Every reference to it is a read — `src/fine_art_archive/api/store.py:112` and
`:120`, and `src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py:427-453` — and the file is not committed.
So on any fresh clone pointed at a real works tree, the app starts with zero navigable works and
`/healthz` says `ok: true`. The endpoint that exists to catch navigation loss is blind in precisely
the configuration every new deployment starts in.

Independently confirmed by two adversarial reviewers on 2026-08-23 (codex, confidence 0.99, ranked
it "most serious"; artifact at `Code/Audits/Fine-Art-Archive/2026-08-23-assets/`).

## Scope

- `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py` — make the empty-manifest allowance conditional on there being nothing to navigate
- `tests/test_healthz_manifest_drift.py` — add the populated-archive-with-empty-manifest case

## Non-Goals

- Do **not** change `manifest.csv`'s schema, columns, or storage format.
- Do **not** add a manifest regeneration call in this issue — that is separate work; this issue only makes health tell the truth about the state.
- Do **not** remove or weaken the fresh-checkout allowance. `tests/test_healthz_manifest_drift.py::test_absent_manifest_is_not_configured_not_drifted` must still pass unchanged.
- Do **not** add a human approval, review or check-in step anywhere in this path.
- **Scaffold is forbidden.** A `TODO`, a stub, a comment describing the fix, or a threshold that can never fire does **NOT count as done**. Shipping the test without the behaviour change, or the behaviour change without the test, is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py` replace the `manifest_loaded == 0` short-circuit so the allowance also requires `sidecar_works` to be at most the single shipped fixture sidecar
- [ ] Keep the existing `manifest_drift == 0` arm of `drift_is_healthy` unchanged in `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py`
- [ ] Update the comment block at `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:190-199` to state that an empty manifest over a populated tree is total navigation loss, not "not configured"
- [ ] Add `test_empty_manifest_over_populated_archive_is_not_healthy` to `tests/test_healthz_manifest_drift.py` using the existing `archive` fixture with `sidecars=3411, manifest_rows=0`
- [ ] Assert in that test that `manifest_loaded` is 0, `sidecar_works` is 3411, and `ok` is `False`
- [ ] Confirm `tests/test_healthz_manifest_drift.py::test_absent_manifest_is_not_configured_not_drifted` still passes with its one-sidecar fixture

## Acceptance Criteria

**Named test gate:**
`pytest tests/test_healthz_manifest_drift.py::test_empty_manifest_over_populated_archive_is_not_healthy`

1. That node id **fails** against `6b45762` before the change. Verified 2026-08-23 on a scratch
   clone: `assert True is False` at the `ok is False` assertion, `1 failed`.
2. It **passes** after the change. Verified with the candidate one-condition fix: `1 passed`.
3. `pytest tests/test_healthz_manifest_drift.py` reports **6 passed** after the change (5 today),
   so the fresh-checkout and unreadable-tree allowances are retained rather than traded away.
4. **Deliberate-break demonstration, already performed and to be reproduced in the PR:** revert only
   the `drift_is_healthy` line in `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py` and re-run the named node id —
   it must return to `1 failed` with the same `ok is False` assertion; then restore the fix and
   re-run for `1 passed`. Both outputs quoted in the PR body. Verified on 2026-08-23: fix → `1
   passed`; deliberately break by reverting that one line → `1 failed`; existing suite `5 passed`
   throughout.
5. `python3 -m pytest tests/test_companion_app_config.py tests/test_healthz_manifest_drift.py`
   reports no new failures.
title: /healthz reports ok:true when the manifest is empty over a populated archive

body:
## Why

In the 2026-08-24 archive audit the work-Q-ID check reported **no** shared work Q-IDs while its own adjacent measures implied exactly two. `build_weekly_review.py`, reading the same sidecar tree minutes later, found and named those two. A check that cannot see a collision its own arithmetic implies is reporting a clean bill of health it has not earned.

## Scope

Version the read-only collision audit that emits the `valid_work_qid`, `distinct_work_qids`, `qids_on_multiple`, and `extra_assignments` measures for a sidecar corpus. The audit must count every sidecar that currently asserts `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q`, including variant holdings and ambiguous mutual pairs. This issue fixes the counter only; it does not mutate sidecar data.

## Non-Goals

- Do not resolve the Tintoretto or van Gogh duplicate pairs in live sidecars.
- Do not version or rebuild the historical local-only `build_weekly_review.py` weekly JSON builder.
- Do not change resolver eligibility rules in `VariantLinks.may_hold_work_qid`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `src/fine_art_archive/identity/work_qid_collision_audit.py` with `measure_work_qid_collisions()` that counts every asserted work Q-ID, including mutual variant pairs.
- [ ] Add `scripts/audit_work_qid_collisions.py` to emit a versioned JSON report with `measures` and `worst_offenders`.
- [ ] Add regression tests in `tests/test_work_qid_collision_audit.py` reproducing the Tintoretto mutual-variant pair and the van Gogh unlinked duplicate pair from the 2026-08-24 audit evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_work_qid_collision_audit.py -q --no-cov` passes and reports `qids_on_multiple == 2` and `extra_assignments == 2` on the combined four-sidecar fixture described in the issue evidence.
- [ ] `python3 scripts/audit_work_qid_collisions.py <fixture-root>` prints JSON whose `measures.qids_on_multiple` matches `measure_work_qid_collisions()` for the same corpus.

## Implementation Notes

From the same finding's measures block (audit ts `2026-08-24T14:09:15+00:00`):

| measure | value |
|---|---|
| `sidecars` | 3461 |
| `valid_work_qid` | 2825 |
| `distinct_work_qids` | 2823 |
| `absent` | 636 |
| `qids_on_multiple` | **0** |
| `extra_assignments` | **0** |
| `worst_offenders` | `{}` |

`2825 valid - 2823 distinct = 2` extra assignments. The check reports 0.

Confirmed shared Q-IDs from the same date:

**Q19904859** — mutual partial-crop variant pair (`0777183-…` / `7c89c9a-…`).

**Q24020196** — duplicate ingest pair with no variant links (`569ac23-…` / `8716d0e-…`).

Likely mechanism: excluding variant-linked or ambiguous sidecars from the collision denominator makes mutual pairs disappear entirely. The versioned audit must not apply resolver eligibility filters when counting existing assignments.

Related versioned code: `scripts/classify_shared_work_qids.py`, `src/fine_art_archive/identity/work_qid_uniqueness.py`, `src/fine_art_archive/identity/variants.py`.

body:
## Why (verified evidence)

`stranske/Fine-Art-Archive` tracks a root `node_modules/` tree that nothing depends on, inflating every clone, CI checkout and agent worktree of the repo.

- **`node_modules/` at the repo root is tracked: 356 files, 7,353,094 bytes** — 6.0% of the repo's 121,947,425 tracked bytes. Verified via `GET /repos/stranske/Fine-Art-Archive/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1`.
- **There is no `package.json` anywhere at the repo root**, so the tree cannot even be reinstalled reproducibly from it. It is residue from `npm install --no-save`, which by definition writes no manifest.
- **Nothing consumes it.** `.github/workflows/pr-00-gate.yml:521` runs `npm install --no-save --no-package-lock @octokit/rest @octokit/auth-app` at job time, so CI installs `@octokit` fresh rather than reading the committed copy. The tracked tree's top-level packages are exactly the `@octokit` dependency closure (`@octokit`, `before-after-hook`, `fast-content-type-parse`, `toad-cache`, `universal-github-app-jwt`, `universal-user-agent`).
- **`.gitignore:33`** is the end of the file and contains no `node_modules` pattern, so nothing prevents the tree growing back.
- `tests/__pycache__` is tracked (15,088B) even though `__pycache__/` is already in `.gitignore` — an ignore rule does not untrack what is already committed.

### The one thing that must not break

`.github/scripts/node_modules/` (84 files) is **deliberately vendored** and must stay tracked:

- `.github/scripts/package.json` declares `"minimatch": "file:node_modules/minimatch"` — a self-referential `file:` dependency on the committed tree.
- `.github/workflows/agents-auto-pilot.yml:207-208` copies `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.github/scripts/node_modules` into `workflows-lib/`.
- `.github/workflows/agents-guard.yml:81-82,151-152` allowlists `.github/scripts/node_modules/minimatch` as a protected path.

A bare `node_modules/` ignore pattern matches at **every depth** and would swallow this tree, breaking auto-pilot and the guard. The pattern added below is root-anchored (`/node_modules/`).

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `/node_modules/` (root-anchored, leading slash **required**) to `.gitignore` after line 33, with a comment naming why it is anchored.
- [ ] `git rm -r --cached node_modules` — untracks 356 files / 7,353,094 bytes from HEAD.
- [ ] `git rm -r --cached tests/__pycache__` — 15,088B, already matched by `.gitignore:14` (`__pycache__/`) yet still tracked.
- [ ] Add `tests/test_repo_hygiene.py` with the named test below.

## Test gate

- **Named test:** `tests/test_repo_hygiene.py::test_generated_dirs_untracked_and_vendored_preserved`, asserting all four:
  1. `git ls-files node_modules` returns **no** paths (root tree untracked).
  2. `git ls-files .github/scripts/node_modules` returns **at least one** path (vendored tree still tracked).
  3. `git check-ignore -q node_modules/probe.js` **succeeds** (root tree is ignored going forward).
  4. `git check-ignore -q .github/scripts/node_modules/minimatch/package.json` **fails** (vendored tree is NOT ignored).
- **Deliberate-break → revert:** change the `.gitignore` entry from `/node_modules/` to a bare `node_modules/`, run the named test, confirm **assertion 4 FAILS** (the vendored tree becomes ignored), then revert to `/node_modules/` and confirm the test passes again.

## Non-Goals

- Do **NOT** untrack, ignore, move or modify `.github/scripts/node_modules/` or `.github/scripts/package.json` — see the evidence above; both are load-bearing.
- Do **NOT** rewrite git history. `git rm -r --cached` shrinks HEAD, clones and archives; shrinking history needs `git-filter-repo` and a force-push that rebases every open PR, and is deliberately out of scope.
- Do **NOT** add a bare `node_modules/` pattern anywhere, including a global or nested `.gitignore`.
- Do **NOT** propagate the full `BEGIN/END WORKFLOWS STATUS FILES` managed block — this repo's `.gitignore` does not currently carry it, and adding it is a separate change.
- Do **NOT** change any workflow file.
- No scaffolding / TODO-only changes; every task is a concrete edit verified by the gate above.

_Surfaced by the Orchestrator consumer-sync ingest's repo-hygiene report (2026-08-20), which reads each consumer repo through the git tree API. Verified against `GET /repos/stranske/Fine-Art-Archive/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1` and the cited workflow lines. Prevention for newly-created repos is stranske/Workflows#3145, which adds the same root-anchored pattern to the consumer template; this issue removes what is already tracked here._

body:
Found by the weekly archive audit, 2026-08-17.

`render_weekly_review.py` writes two renderings of the same page:

- `docs/reports/weekly_review_<date>.html` — the dated standalone file
- `docs/reports/weekly_review/index.html` — the copy meant to be served over HTTP

Both emit the **same relative image markup**, `src="thumbs/<hash>.jpg"`, but they sit in different directories, so that path resolves differently:

| page | `thumbs/` resolves to | result |
|---|---|---|
| `weekly_review/index.html` | `docs/reports/weekly_review/thumbs/` — where the renderer copies them | works |
| `weekly_review_<date>.html` | `docs/reports/thumbs/` — **did not exist** | all 23 images broken |

The thumbnails `make_review_thumbs.py` actually produces live in `docs/reports/thumbs_<date>/` (see `thumbmap_<date>.json`); the renderer copies them to `weekly_review/thumbs/` for the served copy and never provides a path that satisfies the dated file.

This matters because the dated file is the artifact the weekly driver is instructed to open, and it is the one that gets kept and referred back to. A decision page whose evidence images are all broken is not actionable — which is the specific failure the "verify before opening" step exists to catch. `weekly_review_2026-08-12.html` has the same defect.

**Workaround applied 2026-08-17** (in-workspace, reversible, no library change): `docs/reports/thumbs` -> symlink -> `thumbs_2026-08-17`. That makes today's dated page resolve, but it is wrong by construction — it can only ever point at one date, so every older dated page still breaks, and next week's run has to re-point it.

**Suggested fix:** have the dated page reference `thumbs_<date>/` directly, which already exists and is date-unique, and drop the symlink. The served copy can keep `thumbs/` since the renderer controls that directory.

Verification for both renderings: `automation_logs/weekly_2026-08-17_verify_page.py` (takes `dated` or `served`); it checks that every referenced image exists AND is materialised rather than a Dropbox cloud-only stub, and reconciles the page's counts against `operations.log` and the live `Art/works` count.

Related: #525, #524 (both weekly-decision-page defects found the same way).

body:
Found by the weekly archive audit, 2026-08-17. `audit_checks/variant_identity` reports **BROKEN**: 21 variant holdings assert a work Q-ID of their own (of 105 holdings). Report: `docs/reports/audit_2026-08-17.md`.

The violation is real. **The remediation the check prescribes is not safe, and this issue is mostly about that.**

## The check's prescribed fix is wrong on 29 of 33 rows

The check says:

> Fix: null `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q` on the holding. It stays reachable through the owner's `files.variants[]` entry.

That reasoning assumes the `files.variants[]` link is true — that the holding really is a crop of the owner. I tested that assumption instead of inheriting it, anchoring every row to the Q-ID's own **P195 (collection)** and **P217 (inventory number)** fetched live from Wikidata, never to appearance. Probe: `automation_logs/weekly_2026-08-17_variant_identity_probe.py`, output `docs/reports/variant_identity_probe_2026-08-17.json`.

Walking `files.variants[]` by `rel_path` (`works/<wid>/master.jpeg`) finds **33** holdings asserting their own Q-ID — more than the check's 21, because mutually-linked pairs appear from both sides. Classified:

| verdict | rows | what nulling the holding's Q-ID would do |
|---|---|---|
| `FALSE_VARIANT` — holding and owner are **different paintings** | 11 | destroys a correct, accession-anchored identity |
| `OWNER_NO_QID` — owner has no Q-ID at all | 18 | removes the pair's **only** identity |
| `TRUE_CROP` — both sides assert the same Q-ID | 4 | correct; the holding's copy is redundant |
| `UNCERTAIN` | 0 | — |

So the prescribed fix is right on **4 of 33** and destructive on the other **29**.

## The FALSE_VARIANT rows are same-title, different-painting pairs

Each of these is linked as master/display-crop, i.e. an assertion of sameness, but the two Q-IDs sit in different museums under different accession numbers:

- **Munch, *The Scream*** — `0ba0ac6` = Q1132918, Nasjonalmuseet `NG.M.00939`; `94de558` = Q844926, Munchmuseet `MM.M.00514`. Mutually linked as variants of each other. Two different versions; both real.
- **Rembrandt** — `2421181` = Q2872723 *Self Portrait with Beret and Turned-Up Collar*, NGA `1937.1.72`; owner `250f754` = Q3630743 *Self-Portrait at the Age of 63*, NG London `NG221`.
- **Titian, *Venus and Adonis*** — `3db822b` = Q603703, Prado `P000422`; owner `aa40f94` = Q4009572, NGA `1942.9.84`.
- **Monet** — `4a2aa6d` = Q3220338 *The Water Lily Pond: Green Harmony*, Musée d'Orsay `RF 2004`; owner `af948a0` = Q20269443 *Water Lily Pond*, Art Institute of Chicago `1933.441`.
- **Vermeer** — `cf72834` = Q15638014 *A Young Woman Seated at the Virginals*, Leiden Collection `JVe-100`; owner `33ebba5` = Q180788 *A Young Woman seated at a Virginal*, NG London `NG2568`.
- **Constable, *Stoke-by-Nayland*** — `3d4c06f` = Tate `N01819`; owner `4740825` = Art Institute `1922.4453`.
- Also: Toulouse-Lautrec *The Streetwalker*, Dürer *Emperor Maximilian I*, Constable *The Lock*, Boudin *View of Bordeaux*.

Corroborating signal: `4a2aa6d` is 3000×2657, aspect **1.129**, yet its role is `meural-framed`. A Meural crop lands on 1.7778 or 0.5625. It is not a display crop of anything.

This is the **G58 failure mode recurring on a new set** — sameness inferred from aspect ratio plus the 20 MB Meural cap without comparing content or accession number. `CLAUDE.md` says outright that aspect is a hint, not proof.

## Two separate bugs

1. **Data:** ~11 `files.variants[]` entries assert sameness between different paintings. Correct fix here is to remove the false variant link and keep both Q-IDs — the opposite of what the check prescribes.
2. **Check:** `variant_identity` emits one remediation for a population with at least three distinct causes. It should classify before prescribing, and it must never prescribe nulling the only identity a pair has (the 18 `OWNER_NO_QID` rows). Suggested: split the finding by verdict and mark `FALSE_VARIANT` / `OWNER_NO_QID` as not auto-fixable.

The check's own note that the count "oscillates rather than staying fixed" is explained by this: resolvers keep re-deriving a Q-ID that is genuinely correct for the holding, and a pass keeps nulling it.

## Not applied

Nothing was changed. The weekly run is read-only with respect to identity, the probe writes no sidecar, and 29 of these rows need an owner decision on which of the two branches applies before any grant is written. Routed to the 2026-08-17 decision page.

Related: #494, #408, #526.

body:
## Why

`schemas/meta.schema.json:478-499` records a series/cycle relation as `stable_identifiers.part_of_q`, but the schema has no position field. The classifier work in #542 can identify group membership, yet a curator cannot represent member order. This is a current data-contract gap: series-aware curation can avoid duplicates but cannot sequence an ordered cycle or numbered series.

## Scope

Add an optional top-level `series` object with a `position` contract tied to existing `stable_identifiers.part_of_q`, wire semantic validation, provide a metadata-only migration command for evidence-backed positions, and add deterministic curation ordering coverage.

## Non-Goals

- Do not infer order from filenames, directory order, or Wikidata labels without explicit source evidence.
- Do not migrate the local-only sidecar corpus in this PR; produce and validate a candidate/report through the established versioned metadata rail.
- Scaffold-only completion does not count: schema acceptance without semantic validation, candidate migration evidence, and an ordering regression leaves the gap open.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add an optional `series` object with required `position` and optional `position_label` / `source` fields to `schemas/meta.schema.json`, and document that it is valid only when `stable_identifiers.part_of_q` is present.
- [ ] Update `src/fine_art_archive/sidecar.py` semantic validation to reject `series.position` without `stable_identifiers.part_of_q`, booleans/non-positive integers, and unsupported free-form values.
- [ ] Create `scripts/migrate_series_positions.py` to read an explicit QID/work-ID/position mapping, emit a reviewable metadata-only candidate and JSON report, and support `--check` without mutating operational sidecars.
- [ ] Add a series-order helper to `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py` that sorts members with positions first and reports missing/duplicate positions rather than inventing order.
- [ ] Add schema, semantic, migration, and playlist tests in `tests/test_sidecar.py`, `tests/test_series_position_migration.py`, and `tests/test_eink_pipeline.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `python -m pytest -o addopts= tests/test_sidecar.py tests/test_series_position_migration.py tests/test_eink_pipeline.py -q` passes and `tests/test_sidecar.py::test_series_position_requires_part_of_q` rejects a positioned record with no series QID.
- [ ] In the deliberate-break check, temporarily remove the semantic `part_of_q` guard; `tests/test_sidecar.py::test_series_position_requires_part_of_q` must fail because the invalid sidecar is accepted, then the mutation is reverted and the named command passes.
- [ ] `python scripts/migrate_series_positions.py --check --mapping tests/fixtures/series_positions.json --sidecars tests/fixtures/series_sidecars` exits 0 and its report names every changed work ID, old value, new position, and evidence source; duplicate or missing positions exit non-zero with the conflicting IDs.

## Implementation Notes

Keep series membership in the existing `stable_identifiers.part_of_q` field; the new `series.position` object adds ordering evidence without duplicating identity. Operational application remains on the separately versioned metadata rail established for #542.

title: Represent and validate series member position

body:
## Why

`src/fine_art_archive/preference/rocchio.py:113-186` now supplies a measured per-work preference score and `src/fine_art_archive/preference/bradley_terry.py:102-175` supplies pairwise strengths. `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py:117-159` can filter and sort a rotation, but it treats selection as an ordered list and has no diversity objective. This is a current behavior gap: the highest-scoring near-duplicates can occupy a whole exhibition even though the archive already has DINOv2 embedding hooks for visual similarity.

## Scope

Implement deterministic quality-times-diversity subset selection for a bounded exhibition. Build a DPP-style kernel `L = diag(Q) · D · diag(Q)` from normalized preference quality and caller-supplied image embeddings, expose diagnostics, and integrate the selector as an explicit playlist mode.

## Non-Goals

- Do not add or train a new embedding model; accept versioned/caller-supplied embeddings through a narrow interface.
- Do not replace ordinary playlist filters or claim cross-component Bradley-Terry scores are comparable when `BradleyTerryResult.comparable` is false.
- Scaffold-only completion does not count: a new module that is not wired into playlist selection, or a selector whose test never distinguishes diverse from top-N output, is incomplete.

## Tasks

- [ ] Create `src/fine_art_archive/preference/exhibition.py` with `select_quality_diverse()` accepting work IDs, non-negative quality scores, equal-length normalized embeddings, a subset size, and a seed/tie-break contract.
- [ ] In `src/fine_art_archive/preference/exhibition.py`, compute and validate the quality/diversity kernel and return selected IDs plus diagnostics for quality contribution, nearest selected similarity, and deterministic tie breaks.
- [ ] Add a `preference-diverse` selection mode to `src/fine_art_archive/eink/playlist.py::PlaylistSpec` and `build()` that applies ordinary filters first and then selects the requested subset with the new selector.
- [ ] Extend `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py::eink_playlist_preview` so supplied quality/embedding evidence produces the same selected order and diagnostics as direct module use.
- [ ] Add `tests/test_exhibition_selection.py` plus focused playlist/API coverage using hermetic vectors with two high-quality near-duplicates and one slightly lower-quality diverse work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `python -m pytest -o addopts= tests/test_exhibition_selection.py tests/test_eink_pipeline.py -q` passes, and `tests/test_exhibition_selection.py::test_quality_diversity_beats_naive_top_n` selects one of the near-duplicates plus the diverse work while naive top-N selects both near-duplicates.
- [ ] In the deliberate-break check, temporarily replace the diversity matrix with an identity-free all-ones matrix; `tests/test_exhibition_selection.py::test_quality_diversity_beats_naive_top_n` must fail on the selected set, then the mutation is reverted and the named command passes.
- [ ] Invalid embedding dimensions, NaN scores, negative quality, or a requested subset larger than the candidate set produce named validation errors rather than a silently truncated or fabricated exhibition.

## Implementation Notes

Keep the core selector NumPy-only and deterministic. The repository's operational DINOv2 cache can adapt into the caller-supplied embedding mapping without making torch a runtime dependency of playlist selection.

body:
## Why

`src/fine_art_archive/eink/gamut.py:79-91` already classifies each work as `well-served`, `compromised`, or `poorly-served`, and the measured 60-work sample behind #512 found 3 poorly served and 8 compromised works. `src/fine_art_archive/display/render.py:149-173` nevertheless always applies the Spectra-6 color path. This is a current behavior gap: a work known not to fit the panel is rendered as degraded color instead of receiving a deliberate monochrome or duotone treatment.

## Scope

Add an explicit rendering-strategy decision that consumes the existing gamut verdict and selects color, grayscale, or duotone output before device quantization. Preserve the selected strategy in render evidence so a preview/export can explain why monochrome was chosen.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change the gamut thresholds in `src/fine_art_archive/eink/gamut.py` or claim measured device primaries that do not exist.
- Do not purchase or require hardware and do not implement Stage C illuminant-aware rendering.
- Scaffold-only completion does not count: adding a strategy enum or metadata field without changing rendered pixels and proving the named regression is incomplete.

## Tasks

- [ ] Create `src/fine_art_archive/eink/render_strategy.py` with a deterministic `choose_render_strategy()` function mapping a `GamutFit.verdict` plus an explicit policy to `color`, `grayscale`, or `duotone` and returning a reason string.
- [ ] Update `src/fine_art_archive/display/render.py::render_for_device` to apply the selected grayscale or duotone transform before its existing dither/quantize step and preserve the chosen strategy in a sidecar result or returned render-evidence object.
- [ ] Update `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py::eink_playlist_preview` and `eink_playlist_export` to expose the chosen strategy and reason for each rendered work.
- [ ] Add focused coverage in `tests/test_render_strategy.py` and `tests/test_render_color.py` for well-served color, compromised duotone, and poorly-served grayscale behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `python -m pytest -o addopts= tests/test_render_strategy.py tests/test_render_color.py -q` passes and `tests/test_render_strategy.py::test_poorly_served_work_uses_deliberate_monochrome` observes grayscale output plus a reason containing the original `poorly-served` verdict.
- [ ] In the deliberate-break check, temporarily make `choose_render_strategy()` return `color` for every verdict; `tests/test_render_strategy.py::test_poorly_served_work_uses_deliberate_monochrome` must fail on the pixel/strategy assertion, then the mutation is reverted and the named command passes.
- [ ] Preview/export evidence identifies `color`, `grayscale`, or `duotone` for every rendered item and never silently falls back to color when the requested non-color transform fails.

## Implementation Notes

Use the existing `GamutFit` contract and `MONO1BIT` / `GRAY16` palette definitions. Keep the policy explicit and deterministic; the result should be testable with synthetic images and no hardware or network access.

## Why

`scripts/classify_shared_work_qids.py:130-142` currently emits `holder_count` and nests P31 values under `evidence.p31`, while #542's published report contract requires each shared-QID record to expose `n_sidecars` and `evidence_p31`. The merged #544 verifier correctly identified this as a current compatibility break: consumers cannot rely on the documented record shape even though classification and migration behavior are otherwise implemented.

## Scope

Normalize the repository-local shared-QID report contract, its checked-in fixture/report, and regression coverage so every record has the documented top-level fields without changing any operational sidecar data.

## Non-Goals

- Do not modify the local-only sidecar corpus, perform a migration, or change duplicate-candidate disposition.
- Do not change Wikidata classification rules or unrelated workflow infrastructure.
- Scaffold-only completion does not count: the named report-contract regression test and `--check` command must prove the committed report has the required fields.

## Tasks

- [ ] Update `scripts/classify_shared_work_qids.py` `build_report()` and `check_report()` to emit and validate top-level `n_sidecars` and `evidence_p31` fields for every record, preserving any supplementary evidence needed by the classifier.
- [ ] Update `docs/reports/shared_work_qids.json` to match the normalized record contract without changing the ten current QID classifications or local-data migration claims.
- [ ] Extend `tests/test_shared_work_qid_classifier.py` with a regression asserting the accepted field names and rejecting the legacy-only record shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `python -m pytest -o addopts= tests/test_shared_work_qid_classifier.py -q` passes and includes an assertion that every generated shared-QID record has integer `n_sidecars`, list `evidence_p31`, and `work_ids`.
- [ ] `python scripts/classify_shared_work_qids.py --check` exits 0 for `docs/reports/shared_work_qids.json`; deleting `n_sidecars` from one fixture record makes the named regression test fail, and restoring it makes the test pass.

This is the bounded verifier concern from merged #544 / #542. Keep the operational corpus outside this GitHub repository; the change is limited to the code/report contract that provider comparison can verify from the repository.
title: Verifier follow-up: normalize shared-QID report record contract

body:
## Why

Merged PR #493 added `GROUP_P31` / `is_single_work_class()` in `src/fine_art_archive/known_works/artwork_classes.py:53-79`, but neither predicate is wired into writes or validation of `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q`. The post-merge verifier on #493 returned OpenAI **FAIL** and Anthropic **CONCERNS**, and the active review threads identify the missing schema, migration, and collision-report behavior. This is a current correctness gap: group/series Q-IDs can still be recorded as a single work identity, and the existing shared-QID population has not been classified.

## Scope

Complete the remaining, repository-local implementation contract from #408 after partial PR #493: detect series/cycle Q-IDs from Wikidata entity evidence, persist the relation in sidecars, reject series identities in the single-work field, and publish an auditable partition of shared Q-IDs.

## Non-Goals

- Do not deduplicate, quarantine, or delete sidecars; `duplicate-candidate` records are report-only and continue through `scripts/audit_duplicate_decisions.py`.
- Do not alter unrelated acquisition or workflow infrastructure.
- Scaffold-only or partial completion does not count: adding predicates without schema/validator wiring, migrated data, the complete report, and the named falsification tests below leaves this follow-up incomplete.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/fine_art_archive/known_works/artwork_classes.py`, add `is_series_qid(qid, ...)` that reads Wikidata `P31` / `P279*` evidence using the existing entity-fetch and superclass-walk helpers, and returns series/cycle/group classification evidence suitable for deterministic tests.
- [ ] In `schemas/meta.schema.json`, declare the top-level `part_of_series` relation and update the sidecar validation path that accepts `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q` so a series/cycle/group Q-ID is rejected as a single-work identity.
- [ ] Add a classifier command under `scripts/` that scans sidecars, writes `docs/reports/shared_work_qids.json`, and emits exactly one `{qid, n_sidecars, classification, evidence_p31, work_ids}` record for every shared Q-ID.
- [ ] Migrate verified series-QID sidecars, including the Scrovegni `Q547923` population, from `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q` to `part_of_series`; preserve non-series duplicate candidates without mutation.
- [ ] Extend `tests/test_known_works.py` and the relevant schema/sidecar validation tests for the series detector, rejection rule, migration/report contract, and collision-audit reconciliation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/test_known_works.py::test_series_qid_detected_for_fresco_cycle` passes with `Q547923` classified as a series/cycle and a known single-work Q-ID classified false, using hermetic fixture evidence for the `P31` / `P279*` walk.
- [ ] `tests/test_known_works.py::test_series_qid_rejected_in_stable_identifiers` passes: a sidecar with a series Q-ID in `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q` fails validation, while the same relation in `part_of_series` is accepted.
- [ ] `python scripts/<shared-qid-classifier>.py --check` reports that `docs/reports/shared_work_qids.json` has one non-null classification per shared Q-ID, and the collision audit reports zero series-caused collisions with all remaining collisions represented as `duplicate-candidate` records.
- [ ] Deliberate break: reinsert `Q547923` into a migrated Scrovegni sidecar's `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q`; the named rejection test fails, then passes after reverting the mutation. Capture both commands and outcomes in the PR.
- [ ] The implementation PR contains no direct duplicate/quarantine mutation and links back to #408 and #493's verifier findings.

## Implementation Notes

body:
## Why

This is a **verified current break** in the Fine-Art creator-provenance loop. In
`scripts/resolve_creators.py:148-158`, every unresolved outcome that is not
`resolved`, `anonymous`, or `searched` overwrites the existing artist provenance
with `faa:image-search/pending`. That is correct for a missing or unusable name,
but wrong after `scripts/apply_lens_recovery.py` has already recovered a usable
artist name and stamped `field_provenance.artist_qid.source_ref` with
`faa:google-lens/*`.

The current behavior was reproduced on `main`: Lens-recovered names `Hunto` and
`Shiva and Dayal` are classified as `unattributable` by
`src/fine_art_archive/enrichment/creator_provenance.py:236-245`, then
`_apply_outcome` puts both back in `faa:image-search/pending`. Image search has
already succeeded for those records, so this creates a useless repeat-Lens
loop. The missing behavior is a terminal provenance state for a recovered name
that has no safe single Wikidata creator QID.

The original report also named `Oscar Rex`, but live verification against the
current resolver already returns `Q2032921` with an exact 1.00 Wikidata artist
match. That stale subproblem is removed from this issue.

## Scope

Make the existing provenance before `_apply_outcome` part of the routing
decision. A non-empty artist name recovered through `faa:google-lens/*` that
does not resolve to a creator QID must end in a terminal image-search state,
while genuinely missing/unusable names that have not completed image search
must continue to use `faa:image-search/pending`.

## Non-Goals

- Do not change `scripts/apply_lens_recovery.py` or the work-QID resolver.
- Do not broaden Wikidata artist matching or add a special case for `Oscar Rex`;
  current `main` already resolves it to `Q2032921`.
- Do not assign one combined string such as `Shiva and Dayal` to a guessed
  single creator QID.
- Scaffold-only or partial completion does **not** count: adding a constant or
  tests without changing the end-to-end `_apply_outcome` provenance result for
  both named fixtures is not completion.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/fine_art_archive/enrichment/creator_provenance.py`, add an explicit terminal recovered-name reference beside `REF_IMAGE_PENDING`, such as `faa:image-search/name-recovered`.
- [ ] Update `scripts/resolve_creators.py::_apply_outcome` to inspect the prior `field_provenance.artist_qid.source_ref`; for a non-empty name whose prior ref starts with `faa:google-lens/`, route an unresolved outcome to the terminal recovered-name reference instead of `REF_IMAGE_PENDING`.
- [ ] Preserve `scripts/resolve_creators.py::_eligible` behavior so `faa:image-search/pending` remains owned by image search and the new recovered state remains terminal.
- [ ] Add focused Lens-recovered fixtures for `Hunto` and `Shiva and Dayal` in `tests/test_creator_provenance.py`, while retaining coverage for an empty, never-Lensed name remaining `faa:image-search/pending`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_creator_provenance.py -q` passes,
  including new tests proving both Lens-recovered fixtures finish with the
  terminal recovered-name reference and never `faa:image-search/pending`.
- [ ] The existing
  `tests/test_creator_provenance.py::test_null_name_is_image_search_pending_not_final`
  still passes, proving the fix does not terminalize a genuinely unresolved
  no-name record before image search.
- [ ] Demonstrate the deliberate-break gate in the PR: temporarily make the new
  recovered-name branch write `REF_IMAGE_PENDING`, run the named Hunto test and
  observe its source-ref assertion fail, then revert that deliberate break and
  capture the failing and passing commands/results in the PR evidence.
- [ ] A live resolver smoke check for `Oscar Rex` still returns `Q2032921`; record
  the command and observable QID in the PR without adding artist-specific code.

## Implementation Notes

- Current fallthrough: `scripts/resolve_creators.py:148-158`.
- Current Lens stamp: `scripts/apply_lens_recovery.py:47` and the existing

body:
Observed live during the weekly Fine Art Archive audit, 2026-08-10.

## What happened

`growth_tick.py --apply --grant G55 --batch-cap 10` started at
`14:15:32Z`. Target 1 (David, *The Oath of the Horatii*, 13.5 MB) completed in
about 90 seconds. Target 2 (Leonardo, *The Virgin and Child with Saint Anne*)
then ran for **19 minutes without completing**, and was still running when the
audit finished.

It is not hung — it is genuinely downloading, slowly:

```
$ lsof -p <pid>
TCP 192.168.68.55:65330->upload-lb.codfw.wikimedia.org:https (ESTABLISHED)
REG ... /staging_acquisitions/.tmp_1786371471733.jpeg   65,011,712 bytes

$ sample <pid>
_io__Buffered_read -> _bufferedreader_raw_read -> _ssl__SSLSocket_read
```

Measured throughput: **~70 KB/s** (39.8 MB → 40.9 MB over 15 s). Eight targets
remain behind it.

## The defects this exposes

1. **No per-file size ceiling.** Commons originals for large canvases run to
   hundreds of MB. Note the file had already passed 20 MB — the Meural cap — at
   which point it can only ever be displayed via a crop, so the marginal value of
   the remaining bytes is low while the cost to the tick is unbounded.
2. **No stall / throughput floor.** `_http_get` sets `timeout=30`, but that is a
   socket-inactivity timeout: a connection dribbling 70 KB/s never trips it. A
   transfer can therefore run for hours without ever being idle for 30 s.
3. **Head-of-line blocking.** Targets are fetched in strict sequence, so one slow
   giant delays every remaining target in the batch rather than being deferred.
4. **Unbounded runtime for a scheduled job.** G55 authorises unsupervised ticks.
   A tick with no wall-clock budget can overlap the next scheduled run; there is
   no lockfile in `growth_tick.py` that would prevent two ticks acquiring
   concurrently.

## Suggested fix

- Read `Content-Length` first and skip/defer above a configurable ceiling,
  recording the target as deferred (not a sticky reject — the file is fine, it is
  just large). Where Commons offers a scaled rendition, prefer it once the
  original exceeds the ceiling and the scaled version still clears the
  per-device resolution adequacy check.
- Add a throughput floor: abort a transfer averaging below ~200 KB/s over a
  rolling window, and a hard per-target wall-clock cap.
- Add a per-batch wall-clock budget to `growth_tick.py` plus a lockfile so two
  ticks cannot run concurrently.
- On abort, delete the `.tmp_*` partial (a killed run currently orphans it in
  `staging_acquisitions/`).

## Not a data-integrity problem

Nothing is corrupted: acquisition writes to `.tmp_*` and only renames after the
aspect/pHash verify passes, so a partial transfer cannot enter the archive. The
run was left to continue rather than killed, and its promotion stage is scoped to
its own run report under G55.
