body:
Found by the weekly Fine Art Archive audit, 2026-08-10, verifying the decision
page against its own sources.

`scripts/render_weekly_review.py` hard-codes the card headlines as literal
strings. The evidence blocks underneath them are computed fresh each week, so the
two have drifted apart: **four of this week's seven card headings assert things
this page's own data contradicts.**

| card | heading says | measured this week | literal at |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "30 of this week's **99 new works** have no authorizing grant" | 30 flagged, **all false positives** (see #524); "99" is a literal | `:339` |
| 2 | "**No standing acquisition grant** — pick this week's batch" | **G48 and G55 are both standing**; G55 authorised this week's growth | `:183`, `:353` |
| 3 | "The frontier cap is **starving two of three generators**" | **fixed and measured fixed**: 259 / 133 / 8 admitted per generator today | `:367` |
| 6 | "**138** work Q-IDs are on more than one sidecar" | **88 raw**, of which **11** unresolved; the page's own JSON says 88 | `:323`, `:408` |

Card 6 is the clearest case: `weekly_review_2026-08-10.json` carries
`collisions.qids_on_multiple = 88` and the heading rendered from the same file
says 138.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than tolerating

The page exists because "the report alone is not actionable" — it is the surface
where owner decisions get made. A heading that overstates a defect invites a
decision that is not needed (card 1 invites a retrospective grant for promotions
that are already granted; card 2 invites issuing a standing grant that already
exists twice). A heading that understates progress hides work that is done
(card 3). Either way the page costs owner attention instead of saving it, and the
owner has no way to tell which headings are live and which are fossils.

It also silently punishes the fixes: `merge_candidates()` was reworked to
allocate the discovery budget per generator with surplus redistribution, and it
demonstrably worked this week — but the page still reports the pre-fix symptom.

## Proposed fix

1. Derive every headline from the same `weekly_review_<date>.json` the evidence
   block is rendered from. No count, artist name, or "no such grant exists"
   claim should appear in the template as a literal.
2. Where a card's premise can be resolved (a grant now exists, a generator cap
   is fixed), the card should **not render at all** rather than render with a
   stale headline — a decision page should only carry open decisions.
3. Add a rendering assertion: every integer in a heading must appear in the
   card's own data payload. That single check would have caught 138-vs-88.
4. Related, same root cause of stale literals: #524 (`PROMOTION_GRANTS`) and
   #522 (`ALLOWED_P31` duplicated in `scripts/`).

## Interim mitigation applied

The rendered page carried an additive correction banner before it was opened,
covering all four cards plus one piece of evidence the page could not show (the
Skagen master/crop measurement). Script:
`automation_logs/weekly_2026-08-10_banner2.sh`; backups at
`weekly_review_2026-08-10.html.bak-pre-banner` and
`weekly_review/index.html.bak-pre-banner`. `node --check` passes and all 25
decision radios and 57 thumbnails still resolve after the edit. No code changed.

body:
Found by the weekly Fine Art Archive audit, 2026-08-10, while verifying the
decision page against its own sources.

## The defect

`scripts/build_weekly_review.py:41`

```python
PROMOTION_GRANTS = {"G14", "G14b", "G14c", "G18", "G36", "G39"}
```

and line 170:

```python
bad = [p for p in promos if p["grant"] not in PROMOTION_GRANTS]
```

That set is hard-coded and has not been updated since the grants that actually
authorise promotion were written. Result: **card 1 of this week's decision page
reported "30 of this week's 99 new works have no authorizing grant", labelled
"Highest consequence" — and all 30 rows are false positives.**

Breakdown of the 30 flagged promotion log lines, with what `permissions.md`
actually says:

| grant | lines | scope in `permissions.md` |
|---|---|---|
| G48 (2026-08-04) | 16 | **standing** acquisition grant; `write-new` into `staging_acquisitions/` **then `move` (promotion into `Art/works/<wid>/` + `staging_sidecars/<wid>/`)**, 100/month, ≤25/batch |
| G55 (2026-08-09) | 10 | **standing** Track A grant; `download` + `move` into `staging_acquisitions/` then `Art/works/` + `staging_sidecars/`, 200/month |
| G51 (2026-08-04) | 2 | `move` (promote `staging_acquisitions/<wid>/master.*` → `Art/works/<wid>/`) for exactly these 2 works |
| G54 (2026-08-09) | 2 | `download` + `move`, acquire then promote master + sidecar into `Art/works/` |

Every one of the four explicitly names promotion. The audit trail is intact; the
checker's allow-list is stale.

## Why this matters more than a cosmetic mislabel

Grant attribution has been wrong in this project before in the *opposite*
direction — 69 promotions on 2026-08-01/02 logged under G41/G42, whose scopes are
dedup and sidecar edits, which produced retrospective grant G49 to repair the
ledger. `operations.log` is the undo-script prerequisite, so the grant field has
to be trustworthy in both directions.

A checker that cries wolf on 30 correctly-attributed promotions is the same class
of failure: it costs owner review time, and the obvious remedy it invites —
"record a retrospective grant" — would write a redundant grant for operations
that are already covered, muddying the very ledger it is meant to protect.

## Proposed fix

1. Stop hard-coding. Derive the promotion-authorised set by parsing
   `permissions.md` for grants whose operation column contains `move` with a
   destination under `Art/works`, or add an explicit machine-readable
   `authorises: promotion` marker to the grant rows and read that.
2. Until then, at minimum add `G48`, `G51`, `G54`, `G55`.
3. Add a regression test: for every promotion line in `operations.log`, the
   grant named must resolve to a `permissions.md` row whose scope covers
   promotion — asserted against the file, not a literal in the checker.
4. The same stale literal is duplicated in
   `automation_logs/weekly_2026-08-03_verify_page.py:70`. One source of truth.

## Interim mitigation applied

The rendered page carried an additive correction banner before it was opened
(`automation_logs/weekly_2026-08-10_banner.sh`, backup at
`weekly_review_2026-08-10.html.bak-pre-banner`) telling Tim card 1 needs no
answer and why. No code was changed.

body:
Found by the weekly Fine Art Archive audit, 2026-08-10. Two defects in one
finding, and they need opposite treatment — which is why the finding as written
blocks the fixable half.

## 1. The publish-mirror gap has reopened

`audit_checks` "Sidecar trees agree (staging ↔ canonical archive)" reports
BROKEN:

```
comparable_pairs: 3392
identity_divergence: 0
master_without_published_sidecar: 5
missing_examples:
  08c6e1e-springtime-monet
  407684d-asmodea-goya
  8384b37-buffoon-with-books-formerly-known-as-portrait-of-el-primo-vel-zquez
  e04d67b-deposition-of-christ-angelico
  f21406b-winter-at-the-sognefjord-dahl
```

Those are **exactly** the 5 works `growth_tick.py` promoted at
`2026-08-10T12:09:40Z` under G55. Re-measured independently (walking
`Art/works/*/` for a `master.*` with no sibling `meta.json`): 5, and all 5 have
their canonical sidecar present in `staging_sidecars/<wid>/meta.json`.

So this is not divergence and not data loss — the canonical metadata exists and
only the `Art/works` mirror is missing. `Art/works/` is the tree the Companion
App reads, so each of these 5 is a picture with no metadata behind it.

**Root cause is unchanged from G53** (2026-08-05, which published 121 such
sidecars): `promote_acquisitions.py` moves the master into `Art/works/` and the
sidecar into `staging_sidecars/`, and its docstring declares publishing a mirror
"a separate concern" — which nothing owns. G53 recorded that the publish step
"is now part of the weekly task (§4a) so this cannot silently reopen". **The
weekly task file has no §4a publish step.** The ownership G53 asserted does not
exist, so the gap reopens on every promotion. Five days, five works.

Fix: have promotion publish the mirror (or make the tick call
`scripts/publish_sidecars.py`) so the invariant holds at write time instead of
being swept weekly.

## 2. The check mislabels its own defect, and the mislabel blocks the fix

- `github_issue_title` is **"Sidecar trees diverge on identity fields"**, but
  `identity_divergence` is **0**. Filing that title would have misdescribed the
  defect. The severity is driven entirely by `master_without_published_sidecar`.
- `fix_blocked_reason` is **"per-field reconciliation, not a copy; direction of
  truth differs by field"**. That is correct guidance for identity divergence and
  wrong for a missing mirror, which *is* a plain copy — it is precisely what G53
  did, safely, with a validate-before-publish step and `write-new` only.

One finding is carrying two defects with opposite remedies, so the auto-fixable
one inherits the un-fixable one's block and never gets applied.

Fix: split into two checks —

1. `identity_divergence > 0` → BROKEN, not auto-fixable, per-field reconciliation.
2. `master_without_published_sidecar > 0` → BROKEN, **auto-fixable** by
   `publish_sidecars.py` (schema-validate each sidecar first, `write-new` only,
   never overwrite an existing published copy).

and derive `github_issue_title` from whichever sub-check actually fired.

## Not fixed by this run

Publishing the 5 mirrors is a write into `Art/works` and needs a grant; G53 was
one-time and is spent. Carried to the weekly decision page for Tim rather than
self-authorised.

body:
Found by the weekly Fine Art Archive audit, 2026-08-10. Follow-on to #411, which
fixed the allowlist **in the library** and was closed — the defect is still live
in the ops script that discovery actually imports.

## What is happening

Every `scripts/discover_candidates.py` run prints this five times and drops the
class:

```
note: dropping class(es) ['Q93184'] — absent from acquire_batch.ALLOWED_P31,
      so the acquirer would reject every result
```

So **no drawing is ever discovered.** The generator pre-filters against
`scripts/acquire_batch.py:57 ALLOWED_P31`, a hand-typed 12-member set that still
contains the junk #411 identified.

## Verified by lookup, not recall

`automation_logs/weekly_2026-08-10_verify_p31.py` resolved every member live
against Wikidata:

| Q-ID | label |
|---|---|
| Q3305213 | painting |
| Q4502142 | visual artwork |
| **Q11086742** | **anime television program** |
| Q15727816 | painting series |
| Q860861 | sculpture |
| Q15711026 | altarpiece |
| Q11060274 | print |
| Q18761202 | watercolor painting |
| **Q1167694** | **Raboy — a Wikimedia disambiguation page** |
| Q838948 | work of art |
| **Q57276** | **Michael D. Higgins (President of Ireland)** |
| Q179700 | statue |

and `Q93184` = **drawing**.

## The dropped class would have passed the acquirer anyway

SPARQL, same script:

```
wd:Q93184 wdt:P279* ?root  ->  Q838948 (work of art), Q4502142 (visual artwork)
```

Both are in `ALLOWED_P31`, and `acquire_batch.py`'s own gate is transitive over
`P279*` by decision (Tim, 2026-08-01: "accept all subclasses", docstring at
`acquire_batch.py:192`). **So the acquirer would have accepted drawings; the
generator's exact-set pre-check is what loses the whole category.** Two gates
for one question, disagreeing.

The same file already contradicts itself: `WORKS_ON_PAPER = {"Q11060274",
"Q93184"}` at line 67 exists specifically to give drawings a lenient aspect
threshold — a class the line above refuses to admit.

## The fix already exists and is already installed

`src/fine_art_archive/known_works/artwork_classes.py` on `main` has the verified
set — includes `Q93184`, and its comment says it "intentionally excludes prior
junk entries Q11086742 / Q1167694 / Q57276". It is importable from the very
interpreter the ops scripts run under:

```
$ /Users/teacher/.faa-venv/bin/python3 -c \
  "from fine_art_archive.known_works.artwork_classes import ALLOWED_P31; print(sorted(ALLOWED_P31))"
['Q11060274', 'Q15711026', 'Q15727816', 'Q179700', 'Q18761202', 'Q3305213',
 'Q4502142', 'Q838948', 'Q860861', 'Q93184']
```

(package resolves to `/Users/teacher/.faa-lib/FAA-wave2/src/fine_art_archive/`)

## Proposed fix

1. `scripts/acquire_batch.py`: delete the local `ALLOWED_P31` literal and import
   `fine_art_archive.known_works.artwork_classes.ALLOWED_P31`. Same for
   `WORKS_ON_PAPER` if the library carries an equivalent.
2. `scripts/discover_candidates.py`: make the pre-check transitive, or drop it —
   pre-filtering with a *different* rule than the acquirer's is what created a
   silent category-wide loss rather than a visible per-target rejection.
3. Add a regression test that the ops path and the library agree, so this cannot
   diverge again. This is the "library + thin wrappers, no duplicated logic" rule
   in `CLAUDE.md`; a hand-rolled copy in `scripts/` is the thing it forbids.

## Impact

Drawings are absent from growth entirely — not rejected at acquisition where it
would be visible, but never proposed. Given the archive holds Dürer, Rembrandt
and Bruegel works on paper, the missing category is material.

No code was changed by the audit run; acquisition-gate behaviour is Tim's call.

body:
# [audit 2026-08-08][epic] A-series — long-horizon capabilities (A1–A17)

## Why

The 2026-08-08 audit produced 119 findings across four severities. The near-term
ones (N-*) are now largely done: Waves 0–4 are complete, Wave 5 (D4 auto-expiry)
landed with this issue, and Wave 6 delivered the gamut-fit score (#512), the
dither regression metric (#502), the palette sensitivity sweep (#513), the
Rocchio preference vector (#505) and the Bradley-Terry session (#514).

What remains is the **A-series**: seventeen capability epics that were
deliberately deferred because each depended on something that did not exist yet.
Several of those dependencies now do. This issue exists so the A-series stops
being a list in an audit document nobody re-reads and becomes tracked work with
a stated order.

**The sequencing is the substance.** Attempting A12 before A9 optimises against
a panel model that is a guess; attempting A15 before a preference score ranks by
nothing. Each stage below states what unblocked it.

## Scope

Stage the A-series and open one child issue per item as its stage becomes
current. This issue tracks the order and the gates, not the implementations.

### Stage A — unblocked by Wave 6, actionable now

| item | what it is | what unblocked it |
|---|---|---|
| **A11** | Monochrome-first as a strategy, not a fallback: works whose gamut does not fit get a deliberate mono/duotone rendering instead of bad colour | the gamut-fit score (#512). Measured on 60 works: **3 poorly-served, 8 compromised** — Vermeer's *Mistress and Maid* at 33% out of gamut, Hopkinson's *Coolidge* at 35% |
| **A15** | Exhibition sequencing as quality × diversity subset selection (DPP kernel `L = Q·D`) — treat a rotation as a *set*, not a ranked list | `Q` from Rocchio (#505) + Bradley-Terry (#514); `D` from the DINOv2 embeddings already in the archive |
| **A8** | Series-aware curation: sequence a series, avoid four near-identical members in one week | **partially blocked** — `stable_identifiers.part_of_q` exists (#486/#491) but there is no `position` field, so order within a series is not expressible |

### Stage B — measurable model upgrades

A3 (DINOv3 migration, +10.8 GAP over DINOv2 on the Met artworks benchmark, A/B
measurable on this archive), A4 (aspect-preserving multi-crop embeddings),
A7 (embedding-augmented candidate generation with deterministic commit),
A14 (ground the affect vocabulary in the embedding space).

### Stage C — needs hardware or a spectrophotometer, strictly in order

A9 (illuminant-aware rendering from measured spectral reflectance) → A12
(optimisation-based halftoning against that model) → A13 (own the panel).

**#513 is the argument for waiting.** The palette error bar across plausible
published estimates is **16.6%**, and #502 measured Floyd-Steinberg against
Atkinson at **6.5%** apart. Any dithering work before A9 optimises inside its own
uncertainty.

### Stage D — publication contracts

A2 (Linked Art 1.0 as a pinned export contract validated in CI), A5 (C2PA
Content Credentials on promoted masters and rendered e-ink images), A6
(reconciliation-client architecture replacing bespoke resolvers), A1 (two-witness
reproduction-fidelity corpus).

### Stage E — dossiers and evaluation

A16 (demand-ordered dossier generation), A17 (the archive as an internal VLM
evaluation harness), A10 (content-adaptive rendering driven by the ratings log).

## Non-Goals

- **Not** implementing any A-item in this issue. This is sequencing only; each
  item gets its own issue with its own acceptance gate when its stage opens.
- **Not** re-litigating the audit's findings. The A-series is taken as given.
- **Not** starting Stage C before hardware exists. That is the whole point of
  #513's error bar, and starting early is how unmeasurable work gets shipped.
- **No** scaffolding, placeholder modules, or `TODO` stubs for later stages.

## Tasks

- [ ] Use `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/agent_task.yml` to open a child issue for **A11** (monochrome-first), citing the measured gamut verdicts from #512 and naming the intended implementation path under `src/fine_art_archive/`.
- [ ] Use `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/agent_task.yml` to open a child issue for **A15** (exhibition sequencing), naming `src/fine_art_archive/preference/rocchio.py`, `bradley_terry.py`, and the existing DINOv2 embedding surface as the DPP kernel inputs.
- [ ] Use `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/agent_task.yml` to open a child issue for the **`series.position`** gap in `schemas/meta.schema.json`, including migration and validator tests.
- [ ] Write the stage order to `docs/A_SERIES_ROADMAP.md` so it survives this issue being closed.
- [ ] Run `gh issue view 21 --repo stranske/Fine-Art-Archive` and close or re-scope `#21 [BLOCKED epic] Preference model` against the delivered symbols in `src/fine_art_archive/preference/rocchio.py` and `bradley_terry.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The stage order is written to a file in `docs/`, and

body:
## Why

A work Q-ID denotes exactly one work. `scripts/backfill_work_qids_by_creator.py` matches a sidecar title against the creator's Wikidata oeuvre and writes the best match, but nothing checks whether another sidecar already asserts that Q-ID. When an artist painted a subject more than once, every holding matches the same label at score 1.00, so the pass writes one identifier onto two works.

`backfill()` at `scripts/backfill_work_qids_by_creator.py:216` goes straight from `reasons["match"] += 1` to `_apply_match(meta, match)` with no uniqueness check, and `_eligible()` (line 136) only asks whether *this* sidecar lacks a Q-ID.

Observed in the archive on 2026-08-09 — seven Q-IDs on two works each, all written by this pass at score >= 0.96:

| Q-ID | works | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `Q27955591` *The Feast of Herod* | National Galleries Scotland x2 | sidecar years **1635** and **1425** |
| `Q17277950` *The Card Player(s)* | Cezanne, Courtauld x2 | years **1890-92** and **1892-95** |
| `Q47512039` *Ronald Reagan* | Kinstler, NPG x2 | both 1991 |
| `Q16167060` *Self-Portrait* | Rembrandt x2 | five distinct self-portraits shared this Q-ID before an earlier repair |
| `Q24020468`, `Q20267913`, `Q20275291` | van Gogh / Monet / Sargent | same-title pairs |

The `holder_qid` tie-breaker added in #485 does not separate these: every collision above carries the **same institution on both sides**.

Downstream cost: a wrong work Q-ID propagates into holder resolution, IIIF emission and dossier building, and nothing re-checks it. A missing one merely leaves the field open.

## Scope

- `scripts/backfill_work_qids_by_creator.py`
- `tests/test_work_qid_collision_guard.py` (new)

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT resolve which of the two works legitimately owns the Q-ID by image comparison. No image statistic tested against this archive separates "different work" from "another photograph of the same work" — inlier ratio puts Caravaggio's *Ecce Homo* at 0.022 as ONE work and two Rembrandt self-portraits at 0.029 as two. Collisions are reported for judgement, never auto-resolved.
- Do NOT weaken or bypass the existing match guards (best score, unambiguous, year agreement).
- A scaffolded `TODO` or a guard that is defined but not reached in `backfill()` does not close this. The refusal must be observable in the CLI summary.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `_work_qid_holders(staging_dir)` to `scripts/backfill_work_qids_by_creator.py`, returning `dict[str, list[str]]` mapping work Q-ID to the `work_id`s already asserting it, built with the existing `_sidecar_paths()` and `_work_qid()` helpers.
- [ ] In `backfill()` in `scripts/backfill_work_qids_by_creator.py`, call `_work_qid_holders()` before the `for path in _sidecar_paths(staging_dir)` loop.
- [ ] In that same loop, between `resolve_work_qid(...)` returning a match and the `_apply_match(meta, match)` call, skip any match whose `match.work_qid` is already held by a different `work_id`, incrementing `reasons["already-held-by-another-work"]` instead of `reasons["match"]`.
- [ ] After each successful `_apply_match` write in `backfill()`, append the new `work_id` to the holders index so a second eligible work in the same run cannot take the same Q-ID.
- [ ] Add a `collisions: list[dict[str, Any]]` field to the `WorkQidBackfillStats` dataclass in `scripts/backfill_work_qids_by_creator.py`, populated with `work_id`, `title`, `work_qid`, `label`, `score` and `held_by`.
- [ ] Print `refused_collision=<N>` in the summary line emitted by `main()` in `scripts/backfill_work_qids_by_creator.py`, plus one `REFUSED <work_id>: <qid> ... is already held by <work_id>` line per collision.
- [ ] Add `tests/test_work_qid_collision_guard.py` with cases: refusal against a pre-existing holder; refusal within one run; a free Q-ID still written; a work already holding its own Q-ID is ineligible rather than self-refused.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Test gate:** `python3 -m pytest tests/test_work_qid_collision_guard.py` exits 0 with 5 passed.
- [ ] **Deliberate break:** replacing the guard expression in `backfill()` with `already = []` makes `python3 -m pytest tests/test_work_qid_collision_guard.py` exit non-zero with at least 3 failures; reverting returns it to 5 passed.
- [ ] `python3 -m ruff check --extend-exclude .workflows-lib .` exits 0 and prints `All checks passed!`.
- [ ] `python3 -m pytest --ignore=tests/test_iiif.py tests/` exits 0.
- [ ] Running `scripts/backfill_work_qids_by_creator.py --staging-dir <dir> --include-categorized --apply` against a staging dir holding one sidecar with `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q = Q5712848` and a second QID-less sidecar of the same title prints `refused_collision=1` and `written=0`, and the second sidecar's `stable_identifiers` remains absent.

## Implementation Notes

Refusing is the conservative direction and is correct whichever case applies — whether the second sidecar is a different painting or another holding of the same one, it must not silently take an identifier that is already spoken for.

Implemented in #488.

> **Not dispatchable to an agent — needs physical hardware that does not exist yet.** Tracking only; do not add `agents:auto-pilot`.

## Why

Epic #23 is closed because its blocker (which panel, push vs SD) is resolved and **both** transports are built, tested and merged. But #23's goal says deliver to the *physical* panels, and no panel has been bought. Everything is verified against the app, nothing against glass.

Two specific things are unknown until a real device exists, and both are recorded here so they are not rediscovered:

**1. The palette is estimated, not measured.** `src/fine_art_archive/eink/palette.py` ships Spectra 6 primaries that are reasonable guesses. Every palette carries `measured: False`, and every exported SD card states so in `playlist.json` and `README.txt`. No vendor at these sizes publishes a colour profile, gamut volume or Delta-E — `docs/EINK_DEVICE_SURVEY.md` calls this the survey's central open gap. Replacing six RGB triples upgrades every card and feed retroactively.

**2. Colour may not be good enough at all.** The one independent hands-on report of a 28.5" colour unit describes photographs as "dark, desaturated, and low resolution", with no pure white — only "a yellowish grey" — and **monochrome reproductions faring markedly better than colour**. The survey's own recommendation is to measure a unit before committing the pipeline to colour e-paper. If mono wins, the `gray16` target already exists.

## Scope

First-light verification of the existing pipeline against one purchased panel. No new features.

## Non-Goals

- No new render targets, transports or UI. Both transports are done.
- Not buying the hardware — that is the owner's decision, and the survey's US-availability read is in `docs/EINK_DEVICE_SURVEY.md`.
- Not a colour-management system. Six measured primaries is the deliverable, not an ICC workflow.

## Tasks

- [ ] Photograph a rendered card under controlled light and sample the six Spectra 6 primaries from a full-coverage test pattern; record the measured RGB.
- [ ] Replace the estimated tuples in `palette.py` `SPECTRA6` with the measured values and set `measured=True`.
- [ ] Re-run `dither_error` on a reference work with measured vs estimated palettes and record the change in `perceived_rgb_distance`.
- [ ] Exercise the chosen transport end to end on the device: for SD, write a card with `scripts/make_eink_card.py --write` and confirm the panel plays it in filename order; for network, point the device at `/feed/{id}/current` and confirm it advances across a rotation interval.
- [ ] Compare a colour render against a `gray16` render of the same work on the panel and record which reads better, per the survey's warning.
- [ ] Update `docs/EINK_DEVICE_SURVEY.md` to replace "no vendor publishes a colour profile" with the measured result for the device bought.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_eink_pipeline.py` still passes with the measured palette in place (the palette-invariant tests must hold for real values, not just estimates).
- [ ] `get_palette("spectra6").measured is True`, and a freshly exported card's `playlist.json` shows `"palette_measured": true` with no `palette_warning`.
- [ ] A photograph of the panel showing an exported work is attached to this issue — the observable gate, since no automated check can see glass.
- [ ] The panel is confirmed to advance through at least two works via the chosen transport, evidenced by two photographs or a device log.
- [ ] A one-line verdict is recorded in the survey: colour usable / mono preferred, with the measured perceived-error figures behind it.

body:
## Why

The rotation scheduler excludes works from a wall display using `filter:*` tags. Measured across all 3,411 staging sidecars after the Tier 1/2 + Tier 3 passes, coverage is inverted relative to consequence:

| filter tag | works |
|---|---|
| `filter:religious` | 479 |
| `filter:violence` | 67 |
| `filter:death` | 42 |
| `filter:blood` | 38 |
| `filter:disturbing` | 8 |
| `filter:nudity-partial` | 8 |
| **`filter:nudity-full`** | **3** |
| **`filter:weapon-prominent`** | **0** |
| **`filter:occult`** | **0** |

Three works flagged `nudity-full` in a 3,393-work Western art collection is not a plausible true count. So the archive has effectively **no working nudity, weapon, or occult exclusion**, while the tag least likely to require exclusion has 479.

This is a ground-truth bootstrap problem, not a model problem:

- `filter:nudity-full`, `filter:weapon-prominent` and `filter:occult` are 3 of the 18 tags with **no ground truth at all**, so `derive_calibration_set.py` drops them and `clip_thresholds.yaml` omits them. An omitted tag cannot fire by design (`tag_one` treats a missing threshold as inert), which is correct behaviour and also a dead end.
- Wikidata is exhausted as a source here: P136 returned only 3 `nude` genre values corpus-wide, and P180 rarely carries a nudity statement.
- Title heuristics only catch titles that name it.

**The escape is to stop needing an absolute threshold.** For a concept with a natural opposite, zero-shot CLIP can classify by *which prompt scores higher* rather than by whether one prompt clears a fitted cutoff. `nude figure` vs `clothed figure` is a well-separated contrastive pair; so is `a weapon held or displayed` vs `no weapon present`. Relative comparison needs no labels, which makes this a zero-human-input path to the one tag family where inertness has real consequences.

Note this is already how genre works in practice — `merge_into_sidecar` takes the best-scoring genre prompt — so the mechanism is proven in this codebase, just not generalised.

## Scope

`Claude Project/scripts/vision_tag_works.py` and its calibration/report path. Tags in scope are only those with a defensible opposite: `filter:nudity-full`, `filter:nudity-partial`, `filter:weapon-prominent`, `filter:occult`, `palette:monochrome`.

## Non-Goals

- No new model, no fine-tuning, no external nudity-detection API.
- No hand-labelling: this exists specifically to avoid it (see DECISIONS.md D019 — CLIP output must never become a human review queue).
- Not changing behaviour for the 5 tags that already clear the F1 gate.
- Not touching absolute-threshold fitting for tags that have real ground truth.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a `CONTRASTIVE_PAIRS` map in `vision_tag_works.py`: `tag -> (positive_prompt, [negative_prompts])`. Populate for `filter:nudity-full`, `filter:nudity-partial`, `filter:weapon-prominent`, `filter:occult`.
- [ ] In `tag_one`, decide a contrastive tag by `score(positive) > max(score(negatives)) + margin` instead of by `score >= threshold`. Default margin 0.0; make it a per-tag value in the same YAML so it is tunable without code changes.
- [ ] Mark contrastive decisions distinctly in the proposal record (`"basis": "contrastive"`) so `merge_into_sidecar` and the report can tell them apart from threshold decisions.
- [ ] Ensure a contrastive tag is NOT suppressed by the `--min-f1` gate (it has no F1, by construction) while remaining suppressible via an explicit `--no-contrastive` flag.
- [ ] Emit contrastive tags in `clip_calibration_report.json` with `basis: "contrastive"` and their margin, so the report stays a complete account of what can fire.
- [ ] Preserve the existing merge invariants: contrastive tags rank below Wikidata, never overwrite a reviewer state, and set `needs_review`.
- [ ] Measure the outcome: report how many works each contrastive tag flags across the corpus, and spot-check the top-20 and bottom-20 scoring works per tag to confirm the direction of separation is right.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `python3 Claude Project/scripts/test_vision_tag_merge.py` passes, extended with cases asserting: a contrastive tag can fire with no entry in `clip_thresholds.yaml`; a contrastive tag does not overwrite a `wikidata:P180` tag of the same id; a contrastive tag sets `needs_review`.
- A new `Claude Project/scripts/test_contrastive_scoring.py` passes, covering: positive beats negatives by more than the margin → fires; positive beats negatives by less than the margin → does not fire; a tag absent from `CONTRASTIVE_PAIRS` still uses absolute-threshold behaviour unchanged.
- `python3 scripts/vision_tag_works.py --limit 40` prints a gate line listing contrastive tags separately from threshold tags, and `--no-contrastive` removes them from that line.
- `filter:nudity-full` flags **more than 30** works across the 3,411-work corpus (current: 3). This is the deliberate-break check: if the count stays in single digits the mechanism has not worked and the change must not be reported as done.
- `filter:religious`, `genre:painting/portrait`, `genre:painting/landscape`, `genre:painting/religious` and `genre:painting/still-life` fire on the same works as before (regression guard: no change to threshold-gated tags).
- `clip_calibration_report.json` accounts for every tag in `TAG_PROMPTS` as exactly one of `curated`, `provisional-mixed`, `contrastive`, or inert — no tag unaccounted for.

## Symptom

`scripts/discover_candidates.py` logged five times in one run:

```
note: dropping class(es) ['Q93184'] — absent from acquire_batch.ALLOWED_P31,
      so the acquirer would reject every result
```

**`Q93184` is `drawing`** (resolved by live Wikidata lookup). The generator is silently discarding drawing candidates *before they reach the frontier*, so the archive cannot currently grow by drawings. That sits oddly next to the 2026-08-01/02 Bruegel push, which was largely prints and works on paper.

## The larger problem: the whitelist was never verified

`ALLOWED_P31` is a hand-typed Q-ID set, duplicated byte-for-byte in two places:

- `scripts/acquire_batch.py`
- `scripts/acquire_tier_a_v2.py`

Every label below was resolved by live lookup this run:

| Q-ID | Wikidata label | artwork class? |
|---|---|---|
| Q3305213 | painting | yes |
| Q4502142 | visual artwork | yes |
| **Q11086742** | **anime television program** | **no** |
| Q15727816 | painting series | yes |
| Q860861 | sculpture | yes |
| Q15711026 | altarpiece | yes |
| Q11060274 | print | yes |
| Q18761202 | watercolor painting | yes |
| **Q1167694** | **Raboy** | **no** |
| Q838948 | work of art | yes |
| **Q57276** | **Michael D. Higgins** | **no** |
| Q179700 | statue | yes |

**Three of twelve entries do not denote artwork classes at all** — one is a television-programme class, one is a surname, and `Q57276` is the President of Ireland.

## Why this is the same bug as #373, not a new one

#373 was `CURATED_ALIASES`: a hand-typed Q-ID table where 4 of 21 rows paired a correct display name with a Q-ID belonging to a different person, and `Q352` (Adolf Hitler) rode into 67 Renoir sidecars at `confidence=0.99`. Same root cause here — Q-IDs typed in by hand with no assertion that the identifier denotes what the name beside it says.

The **consequence** differs and is worth being clear about: a junk entry in an allow-list is *inert*. A whitelist can only ever fail to match, so `Q57276` has never let anything wrong into the archive. The damage is diagnostic — the junk is proof the table was never checked, which is exactly why `drawing` is missing and nobody noticed.

## Proposed fix

1. Add `Q93184` (drawing). Consider `Q11060274` print's siblings too — `Q18761202` watercolor is present, so the set is already reaching past oil-on-canvas unevenly.
2. Remove `Q11086742`, `Q1167694`, `Q57276`.
3. **Add a test that asserts every `ALLOWED_P31` member is a subclass of `Q838948` (work of art)** — the same shape as #383, which added `test(identity): verify curated aliases against Wikidata labels`. Without the test this recurs the next time someone extends the set.
4. De-duplicate: one definition, imported by both scripts.

## Note on where the fix lands

Both copies are in the **workspace** `scripts/` tree, which `CLAUDE.md` designates canonical for the ops pipeline (`src/` there is a stale fork). If an `ALLOWED_P31` also exists in this repo's `src/fine_art_archive/collect/`, that copy is the one this issue should fix and the workspace copies should be reconciled to it — I did not check the repo tree, only the workspace.

No change made: the audit does not push code, and item 1 is a collection-policy question for Tim (whether drawings belong in the archive at all).
title: [audit 2026-08-03] ALLOWED_P31 is hand-typed and unverified: 'drawing' missing, 3 of 12 entries are not artwork classes

body:
## Why

The weekly audit (`scripts/automation_audit.py --allow-network`, 2026-08-03) ran 4 independent verifiers against driver steps marked `completed`. **Three failed: steps 9, 10 and 12.** Only step 8 passed.

| step | title | why it fails verification |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | Wire needs_review auto-cascade into acquire.py | `try_recover_artist_from_basename` is defined once and **never called** — the cascade is dead code |
| 10 | Collect test batch of 50 works across diverse sources | 21 permanent failures in `run_20260526T024130Z.json`, **no triage doc** — recorded, never dispositioned |
| 12 | Enrich work metadata (work-QID tail + dependent IDs) | 813 of 3,401 sidecars still lack a valid work Q-ID (76.1%); the step **reported 0 writes** |

Root cause is structural: the old driver did `step.update(result)` — whatever a handler returned became truth. No handler self-report was ever checked against the world, so a step could close having done nothing, and two of these closed while writing literally zero.

**`completed` is a label, not a guarantee.** The project has now been bitten by exactly this shape three times — `canonical`, `verified`, and `completed` — so the durable fix is a verifier gate, not three one-off repairs.

## Scope

The driver's step-completion path and its verifiers, plus reopening the three steps. Does not include *doing* the underlying work of steps 9/10/12 — each needs its own issue once reopened.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT close this by re-running the three steps and trusting their self-reports; that is the failure mode under repair.
- Do NOT mark a step `completed` from a handler return value anywhere after this change.
- Do NOT scaffold: a verifier framework with no verifier wired to steps 9/10/12 does not close this.
- Do NOT silently downgrade the three steps; the state change must be recorded with the failing evidence.

## Tasks

- [ ] Create a verifier-gated transition function that checks verifier results before allowing completion status
- [ ] Replace all instances of step.update(result) with calls to the new verifier-gated transition function
- [ ] Add a verification record structure to each step containing verifier name, verdict, and evidence fields
- [ ] Add a `blocked_unverified` state so a step whose handler ran but whose verifier failed is visibly distinct from both `completed` and `not started`.
- [ ] Write a verifier for step 9 that scans the codebase to assert try_recover_artist_from_basename has at least one call site
- [ ] Write a verifier for step 10 that checks every permanent failure in the run report has a documented triage disposition
- [ ] Write a verifier for step 12 that asserts the write count is non-zero and work-QID coverage percentage increased
- [ ] Reset steps 9, 10 and 12 to `blocked_unverified`, each carrying the audit evidence above.
- [ ] Run the new verification framework against all steps currently marked as completed in automation_state.json
- [ ] Analyze the verification results to identify which completed steps fail their verifiers
- [ ] Document all newly discovered false positive completions in a verification audit report
- [ ] Add a --check step-verification flag to scripts/automation_audit.py that runs all verifiers and reports failures
- [ ] Create a follow-up issue for step 9 to implement the needs_review auto-cascade with actual call sites
- [ ] Create a follow-up issue for step 10 to triage the 21 permanent failures from the test batch collection
- [ ] Create a follow-up issue for step 12 to complete the work metadata enrichment with valid work Q-IDs

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/test_driver_step_gate.py::test_completed_requires_passing_verifier` passes, asserting a handler returning `{"status": "completed"}` with a failing verifier lands in `blocked_unverified`, not `completed`.
- `tests/test_driver_step_gate.py::test_step9_verifier_detects_uncalled_function` passes, asserting the step-9 verifier fails while `try_recover_artist_from_basename` has no call site and passes once it does.
- `python scripts/automation_audit.py --check step-verification` reports **0 steps in `completed` that fail their verifier**.
- Steps 9, 10 and 12 read `blocked_unverified` with a `verification` record naming the verifier and its evidence.
- The PR contains two commits: one showing test_completed_requires_passing_verifier passing with a broken verifier (demonstrating the test can fail), and one reverting it (demonstrating the fix), with CI output linked in the PR description.
- Three follow-up issues exist and are linked from this one.

## Implementation Notes

This is the same class as #404 (a cache keyed on a signal that never changes) and #406/#407 (a field trusted because of its name). The pattern that works, per `docs/AGENT_ISSUE_FORMAT.md` §2, is to make the check adversarial: the verifier must be able to fail, and the deliberate-break step proves it can.

---

<details><summary>Original audit finding as filed (2026-08-03) — evidence preserved</summary>

Filed by the weekly Fine Art Archive audit (`scripts/automation_audit.py --allow-network`), run 2026-08-03T14:09:21Z. Source report: `docs/reports/audit_2026-08-03.md` (workspace).

## Finding — severity BROKEN

**3 steps marked `completed` fail independent verification: 9, 10, 12.** (4 verifiers run, 1 passed.)

| step | title | why it fails |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | Wire needs_review auto-cascade into acquire.py | `try_recover_artist_from_basename` is defined once and **never called** — the cascade is dead code |
| 10 | Collect test batch of 50 works across diverse sources | 21 permanent failures in `run_20260526T024130Z.json`, **no triage doc** — recorded, never dispositioned |
| 12 | Enrich work metadata (work-QID tail + dependent IDs) | 813 of 3401 sidecars still lack a valid work Q-ID (76.1%); the step **reported 0 writes** |

Passing: step 8 (11/11 design docs present locally).

## Root cause

The old driver did `step.update(result)` — whatever a handler returned became truth. No handler self-report was ever checked against the world, so a step could close having done nothing. All three failures above are of that shape, and two of them (9 and 12) closed while writing literally zero.

This is the same class of error as trusting a field because it is named `canonical`: **`completed` is a label, not a guarantee.** The project has now been bitten by `canonical`, `verified`, and `completed`.

## Proposed disposition

Reopen each to `pending` with its verifier attached, so a future run cannot re-close it without the assertion passing. Per `discovery_growth_design.md` §IV, `completed` should require a passing `verify()` and a step should re-open automatically on regression.

Not auto-applied: reopening rewrites `automation_state.json`, so it is proposed rather than executed for review of the diff.

## Note on step 12 and issue scope

Step 12's objective overlaps the work-Q-ID finding filed separately this run. They should not be closed by the same change: step 12 is about the *enrichment step lying about its output*, the other is about the *Q-IDs themselves being non-unique*. Fixing either leaves the other standing.


</details>

body:
## Why

The weekly audit (`scripts/automation_audit.py --allow-network`, run 2026-08-03) found **138 work Q-IDs assigned to more than one sidecar — 234 extra assignments** across 3,401 sidecars, at `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q`. Verified again 2026-08-05: still present.

The count conflates **two unrelated causes** that need opposite remedies:

1. **A series/cycle Q-ID stamped on every member.** `Q547923` sits on 50 sidecars, all Scrovegni Chapel panels — that is the *fresco cycle*, not one painting. `Q27951066` likewise spans 24 *Conquest of Mexico* table panels. These are **not duplicates and must not be deduped**.
2. **Genuine duplicate holdings** — the same work under two `work_id`s. D017 dedup territory. Small clusters (Monet *Water Lilies* ×4, Van Gogh poppy field ×4) are the candidates, though *Water Lilies* is itself a series, so cluster size proves nothing either way.

Until the two are separated, **work-QID coverage (76.1%) cannot be read as "works identified"** — the denominator is wrong, so the figure must not be used as a target in either direction.

## Scope

Separating the two causes and making case 1 structurally impossible. Sidecars under `staging_sidecars/*/meta.json`, the field `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q`, and the schema at `schemas/meta.schema.json`.

## Non-Goals

- **Do NOT run any dedup or quarantine as part of this issue.** Per the first hard rule in the workspace `CLAUDE.md`, a lower-resolution near-duplicate is usually a Meural **display crop**, not a duplicate, and quarantining it breaks a live frame. On 2026-08-01, 26 of 34 proposed quarantines were refused for exactly this reason. Case-2 candidates are only to be *reported*, routed through `scripts/audit_duplicate_decisions.py`.
- Do NOT change the 76.1% coverage figure or set a coverage target; the denominator is the thing under repair.
- Do NOT scaffold: an implementation that adds a classifier but leaves every sidecar untouched does not close this issue.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `is_series_qid(qid)` to `src/fine_art_archive/known_works/` that returns True when a Wikidata entity's `P31` (or `P279*`) marks it a series/cycle/group rather than a single work — e.g. fresco cycle, painting series, polyptych — reusing the existing `_superclasses` walk pattern from the workspace `scripts/acquire_batch.py:167`.
- [ ] Add a classifier pass that partitions the 138 shared Q-IDs into `series-qid` vs `duplicate-candidate`, writing `docs/reports/shared_work_qids.json` with one record per Q-ID: `{qid, n_sidecars, classification, evidence_p31, work_ids[]}`.
- [ ] For `series-qid` cases, move the cycle Q-ID out of `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q` into a new `part_of_series` field and leave `wikidata_q` null where no member-level Q-ID is known.
- [ ] Add the `part_of_series` field to `schemas/meta.schema.json` (top level is `additionalProperties: false`, so it must be declared in `properties`).
- [ ] Add a schema-level or validator rule that **rejects** a series Q-ID in `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q`, so this cannot recur.
- [ ] Report `duplicate-candidate` cases only — no mutation — and reference `scripts/audit_duplicate_decisions.py` as the required next gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/test_known_works.py::test_series_qid_detected_for_fresco_cycle` passes, asserting `is_series_qid("Q547923")` is True and a single-painting Q-ID is False.
- `tests/test_known_works.py::test_series_qid_rejected_in_stable_identifiers` passes, asserting a sidecar carrying a series Q-ID in `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q` fails validation.
- `python scripts/automation_audit.py --check work-qid-collisions` reports **0 series-caused collisions**, and its remaining count equals the number of records classified `duplicate-candidate` in `docs/reports/shared_work_qids.json`.
- Deliberate break: re-insert `Q547923` into one Scrovegni sidecar's `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q` → `test_series_qid_rejected_in_stable_identifiers` FAILS → revert. Capture both runs in the PR.
- `docs/reports/shared_work_qids.json` exists and every one of the 138 Q-IDs appears exactly once with a non-null `classification`.

## Implementation Notes

`_superclasses()` in the workspace acquisition script already walks `P279` with caching and a depth limit — lift that rather than writing a new walker. Wikidata calls need the project User-Agent; `scripts/propose_subject_tags.py:240` (`fetch_wikidata_claims`) is a working example of the claims fetch.

---

<details><summary>Original audit finding as filed (2026-08-03) — evidence preserved</summary>

Filed by the weekly Fine Art Archive audit (`scripts/automation_audit.py --allow-network`), run 2026-08-03T14:09:21Z. Source report: `docs/reports/audit_2026-08-03.md` (workspace).

## Finding — severity BROKEN

**138 work Q-IDs are assigned to more than one sidecar (234 extra assignments).** Work-QID coverage reads 76.1%.

```
sidecars                    3401
valid_work_qid              2588
distinct_work_qids          2354
qids_on_multiple_sidecars    138
extra_assignments            234
present_but_malformed          0
absent                       813
coverage_pct                76.1
canonical_path   stable_identifiers.wikidata_q
schema_pattern   ^Q[0-9]+$
```

Worst offenders:

| Q-ID | sidecars | example |
|---|---|---|
| Q547923 | 50 | `0384509-capella-dei-scrovegni-36-lamentation-detail-giotto` |
| Q27951066 | 24 | `02e577f-the-conquest-of-mexico-table-iii-miguel` |
| Q16167060 | 5 | `2421181-self-portrait-rijn` |
| Q24046967 | 4 | `0fc5922-field-with-poppies-1888` |
| Q1189907 | 4 | `3c31a9b-water-lilies-monet` |

## Two distinct causes, needing different remedies

1. **Series/cycle Q-ID misapplied to each member.** Q547923 on 50 sidecars, all Scrovegni Chapel panels, is almost certainly the *fresco cycle*, not one painting — likewise Q27951066 across 24 *Conquest of Mexico* table panels. These are not duplicates and must not be deduped. What they need is a member-level Q-ID (or a `part_of` relation) plus a schema rule that a series Q-ID may not sit in `stable_identifiers.wikidata_q`.
2. **Genuine duplicate holdings** — the same work under two `work_id`s. D017 dedup territory. The small clusters (Monet water lilies ×4, Van Gogh poppy field ×4) are the plausible candidates here, though *Water Lilies* is itself a large series, so cluster size is not evidence either way.

**Until the two are separated, work-QID coverage cannot be read as "works identified" — the denominator is wrong.** That also means the 76.1% figure should not be used as a coverage target in either direction yet.

## Hard constraint on any remediation

Per the first hard rule in the workspace `CLAUDE.md`: a lower-resolution near-duplicate is usually a Meural **display crop**, not a duplicate, and quarantining it breaks a live frame. Any dedup arising from this finding must run through `scripts/audit_duplicate_decisions.py` first. On 2026-08-01, 26 of 34 proposed quarantines were refused for exactly this reason.

Not auto-applied: distinguishing duplicate-work from series-Q-ID requires per-case judgement.


</details>

title: [audit 2026-08-03] Work Q-IDs shared across multiple sidecars (138 Q-IDs, 234 extra assignments)

body:
## Why

The weekly audit (`scripts/automation_audit.py --allow-network`, 2026-08-03) found the artist Q-ID stored in **two places that disagree**: `artist.canonical.wikidata_q` (the canonical path) and `artist.wikidata_q` (a mirror).

- **69 sidecars** have the mirror populated while canonical is empty — e.g. `00bba6a-wrath-heyden`, `02e9c31-the-fair-at-hoboken-elder`, `0e8fa9a-justice-elder`.
- **1 sidecar** has the two set to *different* Q-IDs: `d735d94-william-henry-harrison-peale`.

Coverage reads **91.53%** by the canonical path against a 98% target — but 69 of the shortfall is data that already exists in the other field, so the number understates what the archive knows while simultaneously hiding a genuine conflict. Two fields holding the same fact with no reconciliation rule means every consumer picks one and they do not all pick the same one.

## Scope

`artist.canonical.wikidata_q` and `artist.wikidata_q` across `staging_sidecars/*/meta.json`, plus whichever writer creates the divergence.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT delete the `artist.wikidata_q` mirror in this issue; other consumers may read it. Reconcile first, remove later under its own change.
- Do NOT auto-resolve the 1 disagreeing sidecar by preferring either field blindly — a conflict is evidence one writer is wrong, and picking a side hides which.
- Do NOT scaffold: a reconciliation function that no writer calls leaves the divergence free to recur.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `reconcile_artist_qid(sidecar)` to `src/fine_art_archive/identity/` implementing one stated rule: canonical wins when both are set and agree; mirror promotes to canonical when canonical is empty; a genuine disagreement is **reported, not silently resolved**.
- [ ] Run it over the corpus and promote the 69 mirror-only values into `artist.canonical.wikidata_q`, appending a `history[]` entry per sidecar.
- [ ] Write `docs/reports/artist_qid_divergence.json` listing every reconciled and every conflicting sidecar with both values.
- [ ] Resolve `d735d94-william-henry-harrison-peale` explicitly by checking the Wikidata label against the sidecar's artist name (see #406's `label_agrees`), and record which field was wrong.
- [ ] Fix the writer: identify what populates the mirror without the canonical and make it write both, so divergence cannot reappear.
- [ ] Add a `--check artist-qid-divergence` check to `scripts/automation_audit.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/test_identity_reconcile.py::test_mirror_promotes_when_canonical_empty` passes, asserting a mirror-only sidecar ends with both fields set to the same Q-ID and one new `history[]` entry.
- `tests/test_identity_reconcile.py::test_disagreement_is_reported_not_resolved` passes, asserting a sidecar with two different Q-IDs is returned as a conflict and **neither field is mutated**.
- `python scripts/automation_audit.py --check artist-qid-divergence` reports `mirror_populated_canonical_empty = 0` and `canonical_and_mirror_disagree = 0`.
- Canonical coverage rises from 91.53% toward the 98% target by at least the 69 reconciled sidecars, evidenced by the audit output before and after in the PR.
- Deliberate break: blank `artist.canonical.wikidata_q` on one reconciled sidecar leaving the mirror set → the audit check reports 1 → revert. Both runs captured.

## Implementation Notes

The canonical path is documented at `schemas/meta.schema.json` under `artist.canonical`; `artist.wikidata_q` predates it, which is why the mirror exists at all. `store.py:_resolve_cached` reads the raw `artist_name` rather than either Q-ID field, so read-time behaviour will not mask an incomplete fix.

---

<details><summary>Original audit finding as filed (2026-08-03) — evidence preserved</summary>

Filed by the weekly Fine Art Archive audit (`scripts/automation_audit.py --allow-network`), run 2026-08-03T14:09:21Z. Source report: `docs/reports/audit_2026-08-03.md` (workspace).

## Finding — severity BROKEN

**69 sidecars have the `artist.wikidata_q` mirror populated while `artist.canonical.wikidata_q` is empty; 1 sidecar has the two set to DIFFERENT Q-IDs.** Coverage reads 91.53% by the canonical path.

```
sidecars                          3401
have_canonical_qid                3113
missing_canonical_qid              288
missing_but_has_artist_name        288
mirror_populated_canonical_empty    69
canonical_and_mirror_disagree        1
coverage_pct                     91.53   (target 98.0)
canonical_path   artist.canonical.wikidata_q
```

Mirror-only examples: `00bba6a-wrath-heyden`, `02e9c31-the-fair-at-hoboken-elder`, `08aa0a4-christ-and-apostles-at-the-sea-of-galilee-elder`, `0e8fa9a-justice-elder`, `0ed54e8-temperance-galle`.
Disagreeing example: `d735d94-william-henry-harrison-peale`.

## Why it matters

Two unreconciled fields mean coverage is unmeasurable without picking a side — which is how three incompatible answers to "how many artists lack a Q-ID" (437 / 329 / 283) ended up in the project record.

## The trap in the obvious fix

"Make `canonical` authoritative" was proposed and approved on 2026-07-31 on the strength of the field's name, and verification against Wikidata **inverted** it: on the Renoir rows `canonical` held `Q352` (Adolf Hitler) and the *mirror* held the correct `Q39931`. Executing canonical-wins would have written a dictator in as the painter and would have looked like a data-quality improvement.

The rule adopted instead is **name-verified-wins**: a Q-ID is trusted only when its Wikidata labels/aliases match the artist name the sidecar already carries. Neither field wins by precedence.

## Decision required (schema semantics, so not an auto-fix)

Either derive the mirror from `canonical` after a name-verified reconciliation pass, or drop the mirror from `schemas/meta.schema.json` entirely. Mechanical either way, but it changes sidecar semantics.

Encouragingly, disagreement has fallen from 76 sidecars (2026-07-31) to 1, so the remaining work is mostly the 69 mirror-only rows.


</details>

title: [audit 2026-08-03] Artist Q-ID fields disagree between canonical and mirror (69 mirror-only, 1 conflicting)

body:
## Why

The weekly audit (`scripts/automation_audit.py --allow-network`, 2026-08-03) found **34 sidecars whose `artist.canonical.wikidata_q` does not denote the artist named in the sidecar** (802 distinct Q-IDs checked; 3,107 matched, 4 unverifiable).

A wrong identifier is worse than a missing one: a null invites a lookup, a confidently wrong value gets propagated. `Q352` (Adolf Hitler) sat on 67 Renoir sidecars for over two months and seeded the Track A discovery generators, so the archive was briefly proposing "more works by Q352". That instance came from the hand-typed `CURATED_ALIASES` table in `fine_art_archive.identity.artist_resolver` (tracked in #373). The current 34 are each on a single sidecar — scattered noise rather than one bad table row — so a table fix will not clear them.

There is no automated check that an artist Q-ID's Wikidata label actually matches the sidecar's artist name, which is why this is only discovered by a weekly audit.

## Scope

`artist.canonical.wikidata_q` and its `artist.wikidata_q` mirror across `staging_sidecars/*/meta.json`, and a reusable label-agreement check in `src/fine_art_archive/identity/`.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT re-resolve every artist from scratch; 3,107 of 3,141 checked are correct and must not be churned.
- Do NOT expand `CURATED_ALIASES` as the fix — hand-typed tables are the original cause (#373).
- Do NOT scaffold: adding a checker that nothing calls, or one that runs but writes no correction, does not close this issue.
- Do NOT blank a Q-ID without recording the prior value in `history[]`; a silent null loses the audit trail.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add `label_agrees(qid, artist_name)` to `src/fine_art_archive/identity/` returning a verdict (`match` / `mismatch` / `unverifiable`) by comparing the Wikidata label and its aliases against the sidecar name using the existing `fold_name` from `identity/artist_resolver.py`.
- [ ] Add a corpus pass that writes `docs/reports/artist_qid_mismatches.json`: one record per suspect sidecar with `{work_id, artist_name, qid, wikidata_label, verdict}`.
- [ ] For each confirmed `mismatch`, null the Q-ID in both `artist.canonical.wikidata_q` and `artist.wikidata_q`, and append a `history[]` entry recording the removed value and the reason.
- [ ] Wire `label_agrees` into the acquisition path so a mismatching Q-ID is never written in the first place — the write site is the sidecar build in the workspace `scripts/acquire_batch.py` and the repo's resolver consumers.
- [ ] Add the check to `scripts/automation_audit.py` as a named check so regressions surface weekly rather than by chance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/test_identity_label_agreement.py::test_known_bad_pairing_is_mismatch` passes, asserting `label_agrees("Q352", "Pierre-Auguste Renoir")` returns `mismatch` and a correct pairing returns `match`.
- `tests/test_identity_label_agreement.py::test_mismatch_nulls_qid_and_records_history` passes, asserting the corrective pass nulls both fields and appends exactly one `history[]` entry naming the removed Q-ID.
- `python scripts/automation_audit.py --check artist-qid-label-agreement` reports **0 mismatches** over the corpus, down from 34.
- Deliberate break: set one sidecar's `artist.canonical.wikidata_q` to `Q352` → `test_known_bad_pairing_is_mismatch` FAILS (or the audit check reports 1) → revert. Both runs captured in the PR.
- `docs/reports/artist_qid_mismatches.json` exists and accounts for all 34 originally-reported sidecars with a non-null verdict each.

## Implementation Notes

`fold_name` in `identity/artist_resolver.py` already handles accent and spelling variants — reuse it rather than doing raw string comparison, or "Brueghel"/"Bruegel" will read as a mismatch. Wikidata aliases matter: many artists are catalogued under a different form than the sidecar uses, so compare against `aliases` as well as `labels`.

---

<details><summary>Original audit finding as filed (2026-08-03) — evidence preserved</summary>

Filed by the weekly Fine Art Archive audit (`scripts/automation_audit.py --allow-network`), run 2026-08-03T14:09:21Z. Source report: `docs/reports/audit_2026-08-03.md` (workspace, not this repo).

## Finding — severity BROKEN

**34 sidecars carry an artist Q-ID that does not denote the artist named in the sidecar** (802 distinct Q-IDs checked).

```
sidecars_with_qid          3182
distinct_qids               802
name_matches_qid           3107
name_does_NOT_match_qid      34
unverifiable                  4
non_person_names_skipped     37
```

## Why this is BROKEN rather than a coverage gap

A wrong identifier is worse than a missing one: a null invites a lookup, a confidently wrong value gets propagated. `Q352` (Adolf Hitler) sat on 67 Renoir sidecars for over two months and also seeded the Track A discovery generators, so the archive was briefly proposing "more works by Q352". Root cause of that instance was `fine_art_archive.identity.artist_resolver.CURATED_ALIASES` — a hand-typed table — and is tracked in #373.

## Current residue (each on 1 sidecar, so this is scattered noise, not one bad table row)

| Q-ID | sidecar artist name | Wikidata label |
|---|---|---|
| Q105616807 | `Crespi, 1681-1691` | Nicholás Correa |
| Q130531 | `Bosch (follower)` | Hieronymus Bosch |
| Q2609071 | `Jan Mandijnc` | Frans Verbeeck |
| Q758925 | `Probably Maria Trip (1619-1683)` | Jan van Bijlert |
| Q344838 | `Santiago de Cuba` | Winslow Homer |
| Q8506 | `Cupid and Psyche?` | Il Sodoma |

Note the pattern: several of these are **not artist names at all** — `Santiago de Cuba` and `Cupid and Psyche?` are title/place fragments in the artist field. Those overlap the NAME_FIELD_CORRUPT class handled in the workspace by `scripts/resplit_title_artist_fragments.py`, and for them the Q-ID may well be correct while the *name* is wrong. Distinguishing the two directions is required before any remediation.

## Known false positives in the verifier — confirm before acting

Names with dates appended (`Vincent van Gogh, May 1888`), reversed order (`Gonzalez Miguel`), and mononyms (`Rembrandt` vs `Rembrandt van Rijn`).

## Measurement caveat, this run

`verified_this_run: 0`, `cached_verdicts: 818`. Despite `--allow-network`, the verifier made no live Wikidata calls and every verdict came from cache. The 34 is therefore a restatement of an earlier measurement, not this week's. **Suggested sub-task: give the verdict cache a TTL, or a `--refresh` flag, so a weekly run measures rather than recalls.**

## Suggested remediation path

1. `scripts/audit_alias_table.py` to locate upstream table rows.
2. `scripts/fix_corrupt_artist_qids.py` with a replacement map where **each replacement Q-ID is resolved by live lookup and gated on the sidecar's RAW artist name** — recall is how the bug originated.

Not auto-applied by the audit, by design.


</details>

## Parent

Follow-up to #373. PR #378 corrected the four known bad Q-IDs and added a static regression map, but its closer audit identified one remaining gap: a future new row could repeat the same wrong Q-ID in both hand-maintained tables.

## Problem

`CURATED_ALIASES` remains a load-bearing manually maintained identity table. The default suite must stay hermetic, but maintainers need an explicit, repeatable check that every curated Q-ID's current Wikidata English label or alias matches the row's `display_name`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a small, testable batch `wbgetentities` verifier for all curated aliases.
- [ ] Add an opt-in pytest network test that checks every row against Wikidata labels/aliases.
- [ ] Keep ordinary local and GitHub CI hermetic; document the explicit command that enables the live audit.
- [ ] Add focused unit coverage for payload parsing and mismatch reporting, so the verifier logic is covered without network access.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One Wikidata request can verify all current curated Q-IDs.
- [ ] A matching label or alias is accepted after the resolver's existing name normalization.
- [ ] Missing entities and name mismatches produce actionable diagnostics.
- [ ] Default test runs do not make network requests.

## Non-goals

- Do not change resolver confidence semantics.
- Do not make the ordinary PR CI dependent on Wikidata availability.
- Do not alter existing curated identity values in this follow-up.

## Validation

- Focused hermetic tests for the verifier.
- An explicit local opt-in live audit against the current curated table.
title: test(identity): verify curated aliases against Wikidata labels

body:
## Summary

`identity/artist_resolver.py` defines `CURATED_ALIASES`, a hand-curated table of 21 canonical artists. **Four of the 21 rows pair a correct `display_name` and `lifespan` with a Q-ID belonging to an entirely different person.** The Q-IDs appear to have been typed from memory and were never verified against Wikidata.

Because `resolve_artist` matches these rows by exact alias, it returns `method=alias-exact, confidence=0.99` — maximum confidence, wrong identifier — and nothing downstream re-checks that the Q-ID denotes the name sitting beside it.

## The four bad rows

| `display_name` in table | `q` in table | Q-ID actually denotes | Correct Q-ID |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pierre-Auguste Renoir | `Q352` | **Adolf Hitler** | `Q39931` |
| Jan Brueghel the Elder | `Q150611` | Ferdinand I, Holy Roman Emperor | `Q209050` |
| Jan Brueghel the Younger | `Q462281` | Paul Hazard (French historian) | `Q285933` |
| Pieter Brueghel the Younger | `Q380732` | Henk ten Cate (footballer) | `Q255828` |

Replacements were confirmed against both the Wikidata English label **and** the lifespan already present in the table row.

## Impact

In the operations workspace this had stamped wrong artist Q-IDs onto **86 sidecars** — 67 of them Renoir works carrying `Q352`. The data has been repaired there under grant G37, but the table is upstream of that, so any future resolver run reintroduces it.

Second-order effect worth noting: artist Q-IDs from the archive are used as seed input to Wikidata discovery queries, so a corrupt value causes the discovery frontier to start proposing "more works by `Q352`". One such candidate was generated before the bug was found.

## Suggested fix

1. Correct the four `q` values.
2. Add a test that asserts, for every `CURATED_ALIASES` row, that the Q-ID's Wikidata label/aliases match its `display_name`. A hand-maintained identifier table without such a test will drift again — this is the failure mode, not the specific typos.
3. Consider having `resolve_artist` cap `confidence` for rows that have never been verified against a live lookup, so `alias-exact` cannot report 0.99 on unverified data.

## Reproduction

`scripts/audit_alias_table.py` in the operations workspace audits the table against Wikidata and prints the mismatches:

```
21 verified OK -> 17 verified OK | 4 MISMATCHED
```

Related repair scripts (workspace-side, data only): `scripts/fix_corrupt_artist_qids.py`, `scripts/audit_artist_qid_validity.py`.
title: CURATED_ALIASES: 4 of 21 artist Q-IDs denote the wrong person (Renoir row is Adolf Hitler)

body:
## Problem

The sidecar schema restricts `rights.status` to `[public-domain, rights-reserved, unclear, fair-use]`, but 4 Art Institute of Chicago works carried `rights.status: 'CC0'`. CC0 is a public-domain dedication, so it is semantically `public-domain`, but the raw value fails validation and (see companion issue) aborted the completeness pass.

Fixed in the data 2026-07-26 by mapping the 4 to `public-domain`, but the **ingestion path is unfixed**: the next AIC (or other CC-licensed source) acquisition will reintroduce a non-enum `rights.status` and break validation again.

## Fix options (pick one)

1. **Normalize on ingest** (preferred): in the acquisition/rights-mapping step, map `CC0`/`CC0 1.0` → `public-domain`; map `CC-BY`/`CC-BY-SA`/etc. → `rights-reserved` (or `unclear`) with the license kept in `rights.evidence`.
2. Extend the schema enum to include a controlled set of CC identifiers (larger blast radius; changes the contract).

## Test gate

`tests/test_rights_normalization.py::test_cc0_maps_to_public_domain` — feed a source record with `rights: CC0`; assert the produced sidecar has `rights.status == 'public-domain'` and validates.
title: rights.status='CC0' rejected by schema; normalize CC-family on ingest

body:
## Problem

`scripts/complete_metadata.py` (and `scripts/complete_holders.py`) call `sidecar.validate(meta)` inside the per-work loop and let `jsonschema.ValidationError` propagate. A **single** pre-existing invalid sidecar therefore aborts the entire run — every work after it in sorted order is skipped.

Observed 2026-07-26 on the metadata-completeness source pass: one sidecar with `rights.status: 'CC0'` (not in the schema enum) crashed a 3,302-work batch ~12 min in. Three more works had `files.master.dimensions_px: [0, 0]` (min is 1) — each would have aborted the next re-run.

## Expected

A malformed individual sidecar should be **skipped and logged** (with work_id + the validation message), and the batch should continue. Optionally emit a summary count of skipped-invalid works at the end.

## Fix sketch

In `complete_sidecars`, wrap the `validate`/`write` (or the whole per-`path` body) in `try/except jsonschema.ValidationError`, record `skipped_invalid += 1` with the work_id and message, and `continue`. Surface `skipped_invalid` in `CompletionStats` / the final print line.

## Test gate

`tests/test_metadata_completion.py::test_invalid_sidecar_is_skipped_not_fatal` — a staging dir with one schema-invalid sidecar between two valid ones; assert both valid works are processed and the invalid one is counted as skipped, no exception raised.
title: complete_sidecars aborts whole batch on one invalid sidecar

Part of the metadata-completeness initiative (design: `Code/Audits/Fine-Art-Archive/2026-07-24-METADATA_COMPLETENESS_DESIGN.md`). Depends on #A (schema) + #B (holder). Reuses merged #248 (IIIF) + #250 (Getty).

## Why
Fill still-absent year/medium/category/dimensions/artist-QID by checking authoritative sources, recording per field whether a value was found (`available`), confirmed absent (`not_available`), or superseded a guess (`conflicting`). Must generalize to ANY holding institution, not just the pilot museums.

## Scope
A tiered, institution-agnostic source resolver + a field-fill pass over the 5 fields.

## Non-Goals
Do NOT hard-code one path per museum. Do NOT overwrite an `available` (source-confirmed) value with a lower tier. Never edit the stale workspace `src/` fork. No `.github/` edits.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add `src/fine_art_archive/enrichment/source_resolver.py` implementing tiers, tried in order, returning (value, source_id, source_ref):
  - Tier A: museum-specific adapter for `host_registry` hosts with an API (reuse `collect/sources/*`), using holder+accession from #B.
  - Tier B (institution-agnostic, no per-museum code): Wikidata claims (P571→year, P186→medium, P2048/P2049→dimensions_original{h_cm,w_cm}, P136→category hint); IIIF Presentation manifest metadata (from `stable_identifiers.iiif_manifest_url`, reuse #248); Europeana API; Wikimedia Commons SDC.
  - Tier C: existing value from filename parse → `unverified`.
  - All calls timeout-bounded + skip-on-failure.
- [ ] Add `scripts/complete_metadata.py`: for each work × field in {year, medium, category, dimensions_original, artist_qid} whose `field_provenance` is not_researched/unverified, run the resolver; set the value + `field_provenance` (available/not_available/conflicting) with source+source_ref+checked_at; on conflict keep the higher-tier value and record the loser in `note`. Idempotent, bounded, writes staging + works, logs to operations.log.
- [ ] Improve **artist_qid** resolution for the ~410-work unresolved tail (a match-quality gap, not a timeout): use the holder museum's record artist link + Getty ULAN (#250) + alias/fuzzy matching before giving up → `not_available`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New `tests/test_source_resolver.py` (all sources mocked): Tier A wins over Tier B when both present; a field found only via Wikidata/IIIF is `available` with the right source_id; a field absent from all applicable tiers is `not_available`; a source value disagreeing with an existing value yields `conflicting` (higher tier kept, loser in note); dimensions parse to h_cm/w_cm; an artist resolvable only via the museum record + ULAN is matched.
- [ ] Full suite green; no un-timed network call in the resolver.

## Implementation Notes
Test gate = `tests/test_source_resolver.py`; mock every source so CI needs no network. Demonstrate load-bearing by breaking the Tier-A-beats-Tier-B precedence and seeing the test fail.

Foundation for the metadata-completeness/source-verification initiative (design: `Code/Audits/Fine-Art-Archive/2026-07-24-METADATA_COMPLETENESS_DESIGN.md`). Do this FIRST — B/C/E record into this structure.

## Why
Sidecars can't currently distinguish a field that was **checked at an authoritative source and genuinely doesn't exist** ("not available") from one that was **never researched** ("not researched"). We also can't tell a source-confirmed value from a filename-parsed guess. We need a per-field research ledger recording status + where/when checked.

## Scope
Add a per-field `field_provenance` block to the sidecar schema + a small library helper to read/write it. Non-breaking: values stay in their existing fields.

## Non-Goals
Do NOT change existing field locations/shapes. Do NOT build the enrichment passes here (separate issues). Do NOT scaffold a generic "metadata framework". No `.github/`/synced edits.

## Tasks
- [ ] Extend `schemas/meta.schema.json` with optional `field_provenance` (object, additionalProperties keyed by field name), each entry `{status, source, source_ref, checked_at, note}`. `status` enum: `not_researched | available | not_available | unverified | conflicting`. `checked_at` format date-time. All keys nullable except status.
- [ ] Add `src/fine_art_archive/provenance.py` with helpers: `get(sidecar, field) -> entry|None`, `set(sidecar, field, status, source, source_ref=None, checked_at=None, note=None)` (stamps checked_at if omitted), and `needs_research(sidecar, field) -> bool` (True when absent/not_researched/unverified).
- [ ] Mark the 2026-07-24 filename-backfilled fields (medium/category/dimensions_original) as `unverified` where present (a one-time helper or documented migration note; do not overwrite values).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New `tests/test_provenance.py`: a sidecar with a `field_provenance` block validates against the schema; an invalid status value fails validation; `set`/`get`/`needs_research` round-trip; `needs_research` is True for unverified and not_researched, False for available/not_available.
- [ ] Existing sidecars (no `field_provenance`) still validate. Full suite green.

## Implementation Notes
Test gate = `tests/test_provenance.py`. Demonstrate load-bearing: add an out-of-enum status and confirm schema validation fails, then revert. Keep `field_provenance` additive/optional so the Companion App and all readers are unaffected.

body:
## Why
The 2026-06-28 non-`works/` triage surfaced place-anchored cultural objects (Chartres rose windows, architecture, stained glass) that the current model can't represent: identity is anchored on a **place**, not a creator, and verify Layer 2 (pHash vs a single Wikidata P18) can't gate an object with thousands of legitimate views. Tim approved the design (`Dropbox/Pictures/Claude Project/site_anchored_category_design.md`, 2026-06-30) but it is "future phase, not yet started." Interim works already exist (`works/75d1fab-chartres-south-rose-window` etc.) carrying a stopgap variant `role: unknown` because the schema has no place-capture role. This issue implements the approved design.
## Scope
Implement the three approved decisions from the design spec: (1) per-medium category enums + derived `site_anchored` predicate; (2) embedding-based verify for place objects (τ≈0.55 against the work's Commons category); (3) first-pass scope = stained glass + architecture (the Chartres core).
## Non-Goals
Do NOT pull heritage travel photos (Petra, Machu Picchu) into the model in pass one — they stay in `Others Photos` under the `photograph` category (per Decision 3). No `.github/`/synced edits.
## Tasks
- [ ] Extend `schemas/meta.schema.json` `category` enum with `architecture`, `stained_glass`, `mosaic`, `monument`, `architectural_sculpture`; add a `depicts` block (place-bound identity: site, element, hierarchy) separate from the capture. Add a place-capture `role` value so the Chartres stopgap `role: unknown` variants can be upgraded.
- [ ] Add the `site_anchored` derived predicate (`category in {…}`) used by verify routing.
- [ ] Implement place-object verify: identity-attest via Wikidata/Commons (hard gate) + DINOv2 cosine ≥ 0.55 to any image in the work's Commons category (soft gate); reuses the embedding infra from #193.
- [ ] Upgrade the existing Chartres works (75d1fab south-rose, 52bcc64 north-rose, 6deaee2 stained-glass) to the new category + fix the `role: unknown` capture on 75d1fab.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New `tests/test_site_anchored.py`: a stained-glass sidecar with `category: stained_glass` validates and is flagged `site_anchored`; place-verify PASSES a legitimate alternate view (cosine ≥ τ) and FAILS an unrelated image; the Chartres south-rose detail capture validates with a proper place-role (no longer `unknown`).
- [ ] Existing sidecars still validate; full suite green.
## Implementation Notes
Test gate = `tests/test_site_anchored.py`. Design source: `site_anchored_category_design.md` (Decisions, 2026-06-30). Depends on #193 (embedding infra, merged). Re-tune τ against a Chartres reference set once a corpus exists.
title: [audit][dim6] Implement the site-anchored (place-connected) category + place-object verify

body:
Part of epic #196. Roadmap: `2026-06-28-ROADMAP_dims567.md`.
## Why
Identity resolution today is Wikidata-only. Best practice is to ALSO resolve artists/subjects/places to the Getty vocabularies (ULAN/AAT/TGN) and store both URIs — Wikidata for the broad graph, Getty for authoritative art-domain terms (audit dim 5). This augments, not replaces, the existing resolver.
## Scope
Extend `identity/artist_resolver.py` (and subject/place resolution) to add Getty ULAN (artists), AAT (work-types/materials), TGN (places) URIs alongside the Wikidata Q-ID.
## Non-Goals
Do NOT remove the Wikidata resolver. Do NOT block acquisition on Getty availability (best-effort enrichment). No `.github/`/synced edits.
