## Why
The codebase hand-rolls perceptual hashing (`collect/dedup_cascade.py` dHash/aHash; `scripts/perceptual_dedupe.py` a second copy). Mature, better-engineered libraries exist: `imagehash` (aHash/pHash/dHash/wHash) and Meta's PDQ (`pdqhash`). Adopting them reduces drift risk (see also #188) and improves robustness as a fast first-pass before the embedding verify leg (#193). Audit dim 7. Relates to epic #22.
## Scope
Replace the hand-rolled perceptual-hash primitives with a maintained library; keep the cascade/threshold logic.
## Non-Goals
Do NOT remove the embedding verify leg work (#193) — hashing is the fast first-pass, embeddings are the robust verify. Do not change dedup promotion semantics. Do not touch `.github/`/synced files.
## Tasks
- [ ] Replace the custom dHash/aHash/Hamming in `dedup_cascade.py` (and the duplicate in `scripts/perceptual_dedupe.py`) with `imagehash` (and/or `pdqhash`), behind the existing cascade interface.
- [ ] Re-calibrate thresholds against the library's hash representation; document the mapping.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New test: known near-duplicate pairs are flagged and known distinct pairs are not, using the library-backed hashes; one implementation, imported by both library and script.
- [ ] Existing dedup tests stay green (or are updated with documented threshold changes).
## Implementation Notes
Test gate = existing dedup tests + a library-backed near-dup test. Coordinate with #188 (dedup consolidation) and #193 (embedding verify). Relates to epic #22.
title: [audit][dim7] Adopt maintained perceptual-hash libs (imagehash/pdqhash) for the dedup fast-pass (epic #22)

## Why
The archive uses a bespoke `meta.json` + a custom Wikidata resolver, re-implementing slices of a mature cultural-heritage stack. Several "interoperate at the boundary" moves are cheap and high-payoff (audit dims 5-7; `2026-06-28-ROADMAP_dims567.md`), making the archive portable, viewable, and preservation-grade without rebuilding the pipeline. This is an EPIC tracking several self-contained sub-items.
## Scope
Boundary interoperability with established standards. Each task below can land independently.
## Non-Goals
Do NOT adopt full LIDO / CIDOC-CRM / OAIS formality, and do NOT self-host an IIIF Image API — institutional overkill for ~5k works. Do not touch `.github/`/synced files.

- [ ] **IIIF manifests:** emit a IIIF Presentation v3 `manifest.json` per work (via `iiif-prezi3`) so works are viewable in Mirador/Universal Viewer; pull from museum IIIF endpoints where available instead of guessing max-res URLs.
- [ ] **Dublin Core + Linked Art:** map `meta.json` fields to Dublin Core terms and shape toward the Linked Art JSON-LD profile (Getty/Rijks emit it; consume at ingest).
- [ ] **Dual-resolve identities:** augment the Wikidata resolver to ALSO resolve to Getty ULAN/AAT/TGN and store both URIs (don't replace Wikidata).
- [ ] **Fixity (BagIt/PREMIS):** record SHA-256 per master + a fixity-event log; package with `bagit-python`; schedule periodic re-verification. (Pairs with the canonical-archive hashing — see `Code/Audits/Fine-Art-Archive/2026-06-28-OPS_RUNBOOK.md`.)

body:
## Why
The "Q factor" / display-quality assessment conflates three distinct questions that have three established, separate answers (audit dim 6). `display_quality_design.md` specifies 12 factors; `collect/quality.py` implements 8 (color-depth/bpc and gamut coverage are missing). The bespoke FFT "sharpness" proxy reinvents no-reference IQA.
## Scope
Decompose quality assessment into: (a) DPI-adequacy GATE (deterministic rule), (b) no-reference quality via BRISQUE or NIQE, (c) render-fidelity vs master via SSIM (full-reference, when a dithered render exists). Add the two missing factors (color depth, gamut coverage).
## Non-Goals
Do not remove existing factors operators rely on; add/clarify rather than replace wholesale. Do not touch `.github/`/synced files.
## Tasks
- [ ] Separate the DPI-adequacy check into an explicit pass/fail gate (px ≥ device-native px at intended physical size), distinct from any perceptual score.
- [ ] Add a no-reference quality score using BRISQUE/NIQE (e.g. `piq`/scikit-image/opencv-contrib) alongside (or replacing) the FFT proxy.
- [ ] Add SSIM render-fidelity (render vs master) where a render is available.
- [ ] Add the missing factors: color depth (bpc) and gamut coverage.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New tests assert: DPI gate fails an under-resolution image and passes an adequate one; BRISQUE/NIQE returns a finite score on a real image; SSIM≈1 for identical images and lower for degraded; color-depth/gamut fields populate.
- [ ] Existing quality tests stay green.
## Implementation Notes
Test gate = new `tests/test_quality_metrics.py`. Keep the heavy IQA deps optional/lazy so the suite degrades cleanly when absent. Relates to epic #23.
title: [audit][dim6] Decompose the Q factor: DPI-gate + BRISQUE/NIQE + SSIM + add color-depth/gamut factors (epic #23)

body:
## Why
For a limited-palette e-ink art frame (the "Spectra6" target), the correct fine-art pipeline is: source ICC profile → convert to the device's measured gamut with an explicit **rendering intent** (Perceptual for paintings) + **black-point compensation** → THEN quantize + dither. The current `display/render.py` quantizes by naive nearest-palette without ICC-aware gamut mapping. Doing gamut mapping BEFORE dithering (not nearest-palette in raw sRGB) is the fine-art quality differentiator (audit dim 6; `2026-06-28-ROADMAP_dims567.md`). Relates to epic #23 (e-ink delivery).
## Scope
ICC-aware gamut mapping before quantize/dither in the render path, via Pillow `ImageCms` (LittleCMS2).
## Non-Goals
Do not change the dithering algorithm choice in this issue (Floyd-Steinberg stays default — it is correct). Do not add new device hardware support. Do not touch `.github/`/synced files.
## Tasks
- [ ] Add an ICC step: read the source profile (fallback sRGB), build a transform to the device profile with rendering intent = Perceptual + BPC, apply before quantization.
- [ ] Make the device profile configurable (per device profile entry).
- [ ] Quantize/dither the gamut-mapped image instead of the raw image.
## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New test: an image with a wide-gamut source profile renders with gamut-mapped colors (assert a known out-of-gamut color maps into the device palette region) vs the naive path.
- [ ] Existing render tests stay green; `pip install Pillow[lcms]` available in the dev env.
## Implementation Notes
Test gate = new `tests/test_render_color.py`. Use small synthetic images with embedded ICC profiles. Relates to epic #23.
title: [audit][dim6] ICC-aware gamut mapping before dither in display/render (epic #23)

body:
## Why

The acquisition verify stack's only ACTIVE identity check is **Layer 2: perceptual hash (pHash/dHash) of the candidate master vs a Wikidata/Commons reference** (`src/fine_art_archive/collect/verify.py`). For confirming "is this downloaded master the correct artwork, with correct color?", perceptual hashing is the wrong primary tool:

- A museum master vs a Commons reference differ precisely by **crop / included frame-or-mat / color cast** — exactly the transforms perceptual hashes fail on (a <5% crop can already exceed a working Hamming threshold; ~20% crop → near-random).
- pHash/dHash operate on **luminance only**, so a large hue shift still reads ~97% similar → they **cannot detect a color-wrong reproduction at all**.

Layers 3 (CLIP) and 4 (VLM) are documented skip-stubs (`verify.py:226-239`, default off); Layer 5 (consensus) is missing. The 2026 best practice for this exact problem is **embedding cosine similarity (DINOv2 or CLIP) + a separate color-distance check**, keeping aspect-ratio as a cheap sanity gate. This is the highest-leverage correctness improvement found in the 2026-06-28 audit (dim 6). Shares model/infra with epic #22 (vision tagger). See `Code/Audits/Fine-Art-Archive/2026-06-28-ROADMAP_dims567.md` and `-13-field-research-dims567.md`.

## Scope

- Implement verify **Layer 3** as embedding-cosine identity: embed candidate + reference with a CNN/ViT model (DINOv2 or `open_clip`), compare cosine similarity against a calibrated threshold.
- Add a **separate color-distance check** (e.g. downscaled Lab histogram / dominant-color distance) so a color-wrong reproduction is caught (since embeddings + luminance hashes are both partly color-blind).
- Wire both into the existing layered `verify()` result aggregation; keep pHash as a corroborating signal, not the sole gate.
- At ~5k works brute-force cosine is sufficient — FAISS is NOT required for this issue.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT build the full vision-tagger / subject-tagging system (that is epic #22) — only the verify-identity + color leg.
- Do NOT add FAISS or a vector DB.
- Do NOT change the sidecar schema beyond recording the new verify signals.
- Do NOT touch `.github/` or synced files.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add an embedding helper (DINOv2 or `open_clip`) behind the existing `enable_clip` hook; embed candidate + reference, compute cosine similarity.
- [ ] Add a Lab-based color-distance check between candidate and reference.
- [ ] Aggregate Layer 1 (aspect) + Layer 2 (pHash, corroborating) + Layer 3 (embedding) + color check into the `verify()` PASS/FAIL/UNVERIFIED decision with calibrated thresholds.
- [ ] Make the model dependency optional/lazy (don't break the suite when the model isn't installed; SKIP cleanly as today).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New `tests/test_verify_embeddings.py`: a candidate that is the SAME artwork but **cropped / reframed / color-cast** PASSes via the embedding leg where pHash alone FAILs; a DIFFERENT artwork FAILs; a **color-wrong** copy of the right artwork is flagged by the color check.
- [ ] With the embedding model absent, `verify()` degrades to SKIP for Layer 3 (no crash); existing tests stay green.
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_verify_embeddings.py` passes.

## Implementation Notes

- Test gate = `tests/test_verify_embeddings.py`. Demonstrate it is load-bearing: build the cropped/recolored fixtures, show pHash-only verification FAILs them (the current bug), then show the embedding+color leg PASSes the right ones and FAILs the wrong ones.
- Use small synthetic/transformed fixtures (PIL) so CI doesn't need real masters or network.
- Relates to epic #22 (shares CLIP/embedding infra). This issue is the self-contained correctness slice; the broader tagger remains in #22.
title: [audit][dim6] Embedding-based verify leg (DINOv2/CLIP cosine + color check) — pHash-vs-reference is the wrong primary tool

## Why
`collect/verify.py:157` opens candidate and reference images with `Image.open()` and never applies EXIF orientation. A candidate carrying an EXIF rotation tag is compared with swapped width/height (false aspect mismatch) and a rotated pixel grid (false pHash/dHash mismatch), failing verification for a valid master. Incidence is low (museum downloads are usually EXIF-clean) but the gate is silently wrong when it occurs. Audited at `51a09a6`.

## Non-Goals
Do not change thresholds or the hash algorithms. Do not touch `.github/`/synced files.

- [ ] Full suite green.

Single home for perceptual-hash primitives and for year/separator parsing; callers import them.
## Non-Goals
Keep the two dedup STAGES distinct (name-level vs byte cascade) and the two parsers distinct (positional vs type-classified) — only the shared primitives are consolidated. Do not touch `.github/`/synced files.

## Why
`sidecar.is_valid()` (`src/fine_art_archive/sidecar.py:36-39`) wraps `validate()` in a bare `except Exception: return False`. A missing `jsonschema` dependency or a missing/broken schema file raises `ImportError`/`SchemaError`, which is swallowed and reported as "invalid sidecar" — masking an environment/config error as data corruption. Audited at `51a09a6`.
## Scope
Catch only true validation failures; let environment errors surface.
## Non-Goals
No schema change. Do not touch `.github/`/synced files.
## Tasks

- [ ] Full suite green.
## Implementation Notes
Test gate = new `tests/test_sidecar.py` case; revert to the broad except to show the import/schema-error test FAILS, then restore.
title: [audit][P2] sidecar.is_valid() swallows missing-jsonschema/schema errors as 'invalid'

body:
## Why

Two UI robustness/offline gaps observed by driving the live app at `51a09a6`:

1. **No graceful state when a listed work has no staged sidecar.** The browse list comes from `manifest.csv`; the detail panel fetches `/works/{id}/full`, which 404s when `staging_sidecars/{id}/meta.json` is absent. Observed live: clicking such a work shows a tiny "load failed: 404" toast and a fully **blank** panel — the primary interaction (open → slow-look → rate) is dead with no explanation or retry. Because the browse list and sidecar store are separate data sources that can drift, this is reachable in normal operation.
2. **htmx is loaded from a public CDN** (`src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html`: `<script src="https://unpkg.com/htmx.org@1.9.10">`). In an offline-first personal archive the UI is non-functional without internet and is pinned to a remote, mutable URL (availability + supply-chain risk).

## Scope

- Graceful detail-panel state for missing sidecars; vendor htmx locally.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT redesign the UI or add a build pipeline/bundler.
- Do NOT change the API contract beyond the error-state response.
- Do NOT touch `.github/` or synced files.

## Tasks

- [ ] When `/works/{id}/full` has no sidecar, return a friendly "metadata not staged yet" panel (or omit such works from the browse list, or annotate them) instead of a bare 404 that blanks the panel.
- [ ] Vendor `htmx.org@1.9.10` into the repo (e.g. `src/fine_art_archive/ui/vendor/htmx.min.js`), serve it from the app, and reference the local path in `index.html`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New test asserts that requesting detail for a manifest work with no sidecar returns a handled, non-blank response (documented status + body), not an unhandled 404-blank.
- [ ] `index.html` references a local htmx path; `grep -n "unpkg.com" src/fine_art_archive/ui/index.html` returns nothing; the app serves the vendored file (200).
- [ ] Full suite green.

## Implementation Notes

- Test gate = the new detail-missing-sidecar test (in `tests/test_companion_app_api.py`) + the `unpkg.com` grep check. Demonstrate load-bearing: revert the graceful-state handler and confirm the test FAILS, then restore.
- Observed evidence: driving the app with a 4-row manifest and no matching sidecars reproduced the blank "load failed: 404".
title: [audit] Companion App UI: graceful state for missing sidecar + vendor htmx locally (offline-first)

body:
## Why

`run_acquisition_flow()` reads each staged sidecar with an unguarded `json.loads(meta_p.read_text())` (`src/fine_art_archive/collect/acquisition_flow.py:180`). A single malformed/truncated/empty `meta.json` in the batch raises `json.JSONDecodeError` and aborts the entire flow, so no other valid staged acquisition in the batch is processed. The source-quality aggregator handles this case correctly (it catches and continues); this code path does not. Audited at `51a09a6`.

## Scope

- Make `run_acquisition_flow()` resilient to one bad staged `meta.json` so the rest of the batch still processes.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change the sidecar schema.
- Do NOT silently hide the error — log/record the bad path.
- Do NOT touch `.github/` or synced files.

## Tasks

- [ ] Wrap the `json.loads` at `acquisition_flow.py:180` in `try/except json.JSONDecodeError`, default `meta = {}` (or skip the work with a recorded warning), and continue the loop.
- [ ] Record the offending path so the bad sidecar is visible, not swallowed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New test in `tests/test_acquisition_flow.py` stages two works where one `meta.json` is corrupt and asserts the flow returns a result for the valid work (does not raise) and surfaces the corrupt one.
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_acquisition_flow.py` passes; full suite green.

## Implementation Notes

- Test gate = the new corrupt-sidecar test in `tests/test_acquisition_flow.py`. Demonstrate load-bearing: revert the guard and confirm the test FAILS (the flow raises), then restore.
title: [audit] Acquisition flow: guard malformed staged meta.json so one bad sidecar doesn't abort the batch

body:
## Why

Three related durability/integrity gaps in the Companion App's write and audit paths, none covered by tests (audited at `51a09a6`):

1. **`subject_action` writes the audit event BEFORE validating the request** (`api/main.py:195-218`). For `confirm`/`reject`/`add`/`reset`, a request that then 400s on a missing/invalid `tag` has *already* appended a durable "confirm/reject/..." event → false audit trail + side-effect on failure.
2. **Sidecar mutations are read-modify-write with no lock or atomic replace** (`main.py:193,213,281-283`): two concurrent `subject_action` calls on the same work lose one update; a crash mid-`write_text` truncates `meta.json`.
3. **Corrupt rating-log lines are silently dropped and `/healthz` still reports `ok`** (`store.py:178-187`): a partial/edited `ratings_log.jsonl` line is skipped with no count, masking operational data loss behind a green health check.

## Scope

- Validate-before-write in `subject_action`; atomic + serialized sidecar writes; surface corrupt-log-line counts in ratings reads and health.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT introduce a database or external lock service; an advisory file lock + temp-file `os.replace` is sufficient.
- Do NOT change the sidecar schema or rating model.
- Do NOT touch `.github/` or synced files.

## Tasks

- [ ] Reorder `subject_action` so action-specific preconditions are validated before any event is appended; or write failed attempts as explicit `ok:false` events kept separate from the success audit trail.
- [ ] Make sidecar writes atomic: write to a temp file then `os.replace`; serialize concurrent writers to the same work with an advisory lock.
- [ ] In `_load_ratings()`, count malformed lines and expose the count (e.g. in `/ratings/summary` and `/healthz`); fail health (or flag) when corrupt lines exist instead of silently `ok`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New test asserts a `subject_action` request that 400s does NOT append to `data/subject_tag_events.jsonl`.
- [ ] New test writes a sidecar via a simulated crash/partial path and asserts the original `meta.json` is never left truncated (atomic replace).
- [ ] New test feeds a `ratings_log.jsonl` with one valid + one corrupt line and asserts the corrupt-line count is surfaced (and `/healthz` reflects it).
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_companion_app_api.py` passes; full suite green.

## Implementation Notes

- Test gate = the three new tests in `tests/test_companion_app_api.py`. Demonstrate load-bearing: revert each fix in turn and confirm the matching test FAILS, then restore.
title: [audit] Companion App: harden mutation/audit paths (validate-before-write, atomic sidecar write, surface corrupt logs)

body:
## Why

`POST /works/{id}/rate` accepts malformed numeric input and persists it. `RatingIn.dwell_seconds` (`api/main.py:520-523`) has no lower bound and does not forbid NaN/Infinity; the handler writes the event with `json.dumps(...)` (`main.py:576-577`) which serializes a float `NaN` as the bare token `NaN` — invalid JSON for strict downstream parsers. Verified live: a request with `dwell_seconds: -99` returned 200 and `-99.0` was written to `data/ratings_log.jsonl`. Negative dwell time is meaningless signal, and a `NaN`/`Infinity` JSON literal would be accepted under Pydantic's default `allow_inf_nan=True`, corrupting the append-only log. No test covers these cases. Audited at `51a09a6`.

## Scope

- Constrain rating-input numeric fields and write strictly-valid JSON to the ratings log.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT change the rating taxonomy or the two-axis scheme.
- Do NOT add auth.
- Do NOT touch `.github/` or synced files.

## Tasks

- [ ] Constrain `dwell_seconds` to `Field(default=None, ge=0)` and disallow non-finite (e.g. `allow_inf_nan=False` on the model/field).
- [ ] Apply strict bounds/types to the `quality`/`fit` axes (reject out-of-range or wrong-type instead of coercing).
- [ ] Write the ratings log with `json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=False, allow_nan=False)` so a non-finite value can never be persisted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New tests in `tests/test_companion_app_api.py` assert: negative `dwell_seconds` → 422; `dwell_seconds` JSON literal `NaN`/`Infinity` → 422; out-of-range `quality`/`fit` → 422.
- [ ] A valid two-axis rating still returns 200 and is persisted.
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_companion_app_api.py` passes; full suite green.

## Implementation Notes

- Test gate = the new validation tests in `tests/test_companion_app_api.py`. Demonstrate load-bearing: revert the `ge=0`/`allow_inf_nan=False` constraints and confirm the negative/NaN tests FAIL, then restore.
- Pydantic v2: set `model_config = ConfigDict(...)` or per-field constraints; `allow_inf_nan=False` is the relevant knob.
title: [audit] Companion App: validate rating inputs (bounds/finite) and write strict JSON

body:
## Why

`GET /ratings/summary` (the operator's "Ratings summary" page) only summarizes the **deprecated single-axis** `rating` field. `store.ratings_summary()` (`api/store.py:235-248`) builds `rating_distribution` from `e.get("rating")` and `most_rated_works[].last_rating` from `evs[-1]["rating"]`. But the current `RatingIn` model and UI submit the **two-axis** `quality` + `fit` scheme; `rating` is documented as legacy. Verified live: after the app records two-axis ratings, `/ratings/summary` returns `n_events>0` but `rating_distribution: {}` and `last_rating: null` — the summary the operator relies on shows nothing for real ratings. This is a correctness bug in a read API, not a missing feature. Audited at `51a09a6`.

## Scope

- Make `/ratings/summary` reflect the current two-axis scheme while keeping legacy `rating` for back-compat.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT remove the legacy `rating` field or migrate stored data.
- Do NOT redesign the rating taxonomy.
- Do NOT touch `.github/` or synced files.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `ratings_summary()`, add `quality_distribution` and `fit_distribution` (Counters over non-null `quality`/`fit`).
- [ ] Add latest `quality`/`fit` to `most_rated_works` entries beside the legacy `last_rating`.

## Acceptance Criteria

body:
## Why

The Companion App caches data for the whole process lifetime and never reflects out-of-band disk writes. `store.load_manifest()` is `@lru_cache(maxsize=1)` (`api/store.py:46-52`); `store._load_ratings()`/`_ratings_by_work()` use module globals `_RATINGS_CACHE`/`_RATINGS_BY_WORK` (`store.py:167-205`), invalidated ONLY by the in-process `POST /rate` handler (`main.py:578`). The acquisition pipeline appends works/ratings to `manifest.csv` / `data/ratings_log.jsonl` out of band, and the app is the sanctioned bridge to that data — so the operator sees a frozen archive until restart. Verified live: a fresh server reported `ratings_count=4` for a `data/ratings_log.jsonl` that was empty on disk (stale cache served indefinitely). Under `uvicorn --workers N>1`, a rating POSTed to one worker is invisible to the others. Audited at `51a09a6`.

## Scope

- Make manifest and ratings reads reflect on-disk changes without an app restart, and behave correctly across multiple workers / external writers.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT introduce a database or external cache server. A file-mtime/size check is sufficient.
- Do NOT change the JSONL/CSV formats or the API responses' shapes.
- Do NOT touch `.github/` or synced files.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace the `@lru_cache` on `load_manifest()` with a cache keyed on `MANIFEST_CSV` mtime+size (reload when it changes).
- [ ] Make `_load_ratings()`/`_ratings_by_work()` reload when `RATINGS_LOG` mtime+size changes (drop or key the module-global cache).
- [ ] Keep `invalidate_ratings_cache()` working for the in-process write fast-path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New test `tests/test_store_cache_reload.py`: call `count_ratings()`, append a line to `RATINGS_LOG` out-of-band (not via the API), call `count_ratings()` again, assert the new count is reflected. Same for `load_manifest()` after appending a manifest row.
- [ ] Existing ratings/manifest tests stay green; `pytest tests/test_store_cache_reload.py` passes.

## Implementation Notes

- Test gate = `tests/test_store_cache_reload.py`. Demonstrate load-bearing: revert to the lifetime cache and confirm the reload test FAILS, then restore.
- This is the same staleness class for both manifest and ratings — fix both in one PR.
title: [audit] Companion App: end process-lifetime ratings/manifest cache staleness (reload on mtime)

body:
## Why

`src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:35` hardcodes an operator-specific absolute path in library code:
`ART_WORKS_ROOT = Path("/Users/teacher/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/Pictures/Art/works")`.
Every other path in the module is `REPO_ROOT`-relative; only this one is machine-specific. The result: `GET /works/{id}/image` and `/works/{id}/full` cannot serve promoted masters on any other machine, clone, or CI runner, and tests can only exercise these paths by monkeypatching module globals. `run_companion_app.sh` exposes only host/port, not the data roots. Audited at `51a09a6`.

## Scope

- Make the data roots configurable via environment variables with sensible defaults: `FAA_ART_WORKS_ROOT`, `FAA_STAGING_DIR`, `FAA_MANIFEST_CSV`, `FAA_RATINGS_LOG`, `FAA_IMAGE_CACHE_DIR` (and the store-side equivalents in `api/store.py:18-21`).
- Document them in `scripts/run_companion_app.sh`.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT introduce a heavy settings framework; a small module-level read of `os.environ` with defaults is sufficient.
- Do NOT change endpoint behavior or the data formats.
- Do NOT touch `.github/` or synced files.

## Tasks

- [ ] Replace the hardcoded `ART_WORKS_ROOT` and the other module-global paths in `api/main.py` and `api/store.py` with `os.environ.get(...)`-backed values defaulting to the current `REPO_ROOT`-relative locations (and a documented default for the art root).
- [ ] Update `scripts/run_companion_app.sh` to list the new env vars.
- [ ] Update tests that monkeypatch the globals to instead set env (where reasonable).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New test `tests/test_companion_app_config.py` sets `FAA_ART_WORKS_ROOT`/`FAA_STAGING_DIR` to a tmp path and asserts the app resolves masters/sidecars from there (no reference to `/Users/teacher/...`).
- [ ] `grep -rn "/Users/teacher" src/fine_art_archive/` returns nothing.
- [ ] Existing tests stay green; `pytest tests/test_companion_app_config.py` passes.

## Implementation Notes

- Test gate = `tests/test_companion_app_config.py`. Demonstrate load-bearing: revert one path to the hardcoded absolute and confirm the test FAILS, then restore.
- Keep defaults backward-compatible so current local runs are unaffected.
title: [audit] Companion App: make data roots env-configurable (remove hardcoded ART_WORKS_ROOT absolute path)

body:
## Why

The Companion App uses the URL-supplied `work_id` directly as a filesystem path segment with no containment check. `store.get_work()` builds `STAGING / work_id / "meta.json"` (`api/store.py:118-123`) and the API builds `store.STAGING / work_id / "meta.json"` (`api/main.py:190-193`) and `ART_WORKS_ROOT / work_id` (`api/main.py:296`). A `work_id` of `..` resolves OUTSIDE the intended tree — verified live: `(STAGING / ".." / "meta.json").resolve()` → the repo root. The highest risk is the **mutating** `subject_action` endpoint (`main.py:281-283`), which does a read-modify-`write_text` on the resolved path, so a crafted `work_id` can rewrite a `meta.json` outside `staging_sidecars/`. No test covers path containment. Audited at `51a09a6`.

## Scope

- Add input validation/containment for `work_id` on every endpoint that maps it to a path: `GET /works/{id}`, `/works/{id}/full`, `/works/{id}/image`, `/works/{id}/ratings`, `POST /works/{id}/rate`, `POST /works/{id}/subject_action`.
- Apply the same containment in `store.get_work()`.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT add auth/login or a new framework. This is input validation only.
- Do NOT change the sidecar schema or the rating model.
- Do NOT touch `.github/` or synced files.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a `work_id` validator: reject empty, `.`, `..`, any `/`, `\`, NUL, or URL-encoded separator; optionally constrain to a known-ID charset (e.g. `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+`).
- [ ] After building each candidate path, require `candidate.resolve().is_relative_to(STAGING.resolve())` (or `ART_WORKS_ROOT.resolve()` for image/full); raise `HTTPException(400)` otherwise.
- [ ] Centralize the check in one helper used by both `main.py` and `store.get_work()`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New test `tests/test_companion_app_security.py` asserts `GET /works/..%2Fmeta` style requests and a `work_id` of `..` are rejected with 400 (not a sidecar-404), and that `subject_action` with a traversing `work_id` does NOT write outside `staging_sidecars/`.
- [ ] Legitimate `work_id`s (e.g. `vermeer-little-street`) still resolve normally; existing tests stay green.
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_companion_app_security.py` passes.

## Implementation Notes

- Test gate = `tests/test_companion_app_security.py`. Demonstrate it is load-bearing: temporarily remove the containment check and confirm the traversal test FAILS, then restore and confirm it PASSES; note in the PR.
- `Path.is_relative_to` is available on the project's Python (3.12/3.13).
title: [audit] Companion App: validate work_id path containment (write-capable traversal via subject_action)

body:
## Why

The entire source-quality scoring subsystem (`src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py`, ~472 LOC) has **no effect on production routing**. `run_acquisition_flow()` always calls the routing path with an empty aggregates dict, so every candidate source receives the *same* tier-1 prior and `select_source()` collapses to "pick the first candidate" — not quality-ranked. The aggregator (`scripts/aggregate_source_quality.py` in the ops workspace) *writes* `config/source_quality.yaml`, but **nothing — repo or workspace — ever reads it back**. The same is true of `config/host_registry.yaml` (loader has no non-test caller), `config/sources_seed.yaml`, and `config/known_works/*.yaml`. This contradicts design decision D009 (active-learning source preference must be loaded by the orchestrator at ingest) and means operators editing these configs see zero behavior change. Audited at remote tip `51a09a6`.

## Scope

- Load `config/source_quality.yaml` aggregates (via the existing `source_quality.load_aggregates()`) at the acquisition entry point and thread them into `rank_sources()`/`select_source()`.
- Load `config/host_registry.yaml` (via `collect/host_registry.load_registry()`) and use it for adapter selection + `fallback_chain` (D012) instead of the hardcoded `SOURCE_COLLECTORS`/`SOURCE_PROPERTIES`.
- Fix the now-reachable latent bugs uncovered once aggregates are live (see Implementation Notes).
- If a config genuinely should not drive behavior, delete it and stop writing it — do not leave operator-editable dead config.

## Non-Goals

- Do NOT add new scaffolding, abstraction layers, or a plugin framework. Wire the existing functions.
- Do NOT implement verify Layers 3-5 or the preference model (separate epics #21/#22).
- Do NOT touch `.github/`, synced scripts, or `tools/`.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/fine_art_archive/collect/acquisition_flow.py:166`, replace `aggregates=aggregates or {}` with a real load of `source_quality.load_aggregates(<config path>)` (fail loudly / log if the file is missing or stale, do not silently pass `{}`).
- [ ] Make composite weights / `WARMUP_DAYS` / `CONFIDENCE_FLOOR_WEIGHT` read from the loaded config rather than the module constants `COMPOSITE_WEIGHTS`/`CONFIDENCE_FLOOR_WEIGHT`/`WARMUP_DAYS` (`source_quality.py:59-71`).
- [ ] Harden `rank_sources()` (`acquisition_flow.py:62`) so a NaN/inf composite score cannot sort to the winning slot (use `math.isfinite`; push non-finite scores to the bottom).
- [ ] Fix `_infer_work_class()` year parse (`source_quality.py:248`) so `"1800.0"`, `"circa 1800"`, `"1800?"` yield the correct period instead of `western-painting-unknown-period`.
- [ ] Plumb `check_aspect_ratio` threshold through `verify()` (`verify.py:214`) instead of the hardcoded 0.05.
- [ ] Wire `host_registry.fallback_chain_for()` into source selection so a primary-adapter 404/403 falls back per D012.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A new test `tests/test_source_quality_wiring.py` builds a `source_quality.yaml` where source A's composite for a work_class is clearly higher than source B's, runs the routing path, and asserts A is selected; flipping the YAML so B is higher selects B. (Proves config now drives routing.)
- [ ] A test asserts a NaN composite score is never selected as the winner.
- [ ] A test asserts `_infer_work_class({"year": "1800.0"})` returns the pre-1800/19c bucket (not unknown-period).
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_source_quality_wiring.py` passes; full suite stays green.

body:
## Why

`src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py:305-308` (`extract_signals()`) reads `meta['verification']['source_quality_inputs']` to harvest `phash_match`, `aspect_match`, and `dim_match` from each sidecar and roll them into a `SourceQualityAggregate`. No code in the repo writes this key. `scripts/finalize_acquisition.py:96-105` builds `meta['verification']` as `{**vreport.to_dict(), 'verified_at': ts, ...}`, and `VerificationReport.to_dict()` (`src/fine_art_archive/collect/verify.py:51-63`) returns only `{status, checks[]}` — the `source_quality_inputs` key is never populated. Confirmed: `config/source_quality.yaml` (generated 2026-05-24) shows all 8 real sources at `n_acquired: 0`, `first_seen: null`, and all empirical signals null, meaning zero museum API acquisitions have contributed quality signals. This is **latent fragility, not a current break**: source routing still operates on priors, but when real acquisitions begin the aggregator will see correct `n_acquired` counts with permanently null verify signal rates — the 30-day warmup blend in `SourceQualityAggregate.blended_stats()` (`source_quality.py:170-196`) becomes meaningless because no empirical data ever arrives.

## Scope

- Add `VerificationReport.to_source_quality_inputs() -> dict` in `src/fine_art_archive/collect/verify.py` (after `to_dict()` at line 63) that translates the existing `aspect_ratio` and `perceptual_hash` check results into the `{phash_match, aspect_match, dim_match}` dict that `extract_signals()` expects.
- Wire the new method into `scripts/finalize_acquisition.py::run_finalize()` to write `meta['verification']['source_quality_inputs']` after line 105 and before `sidecar.validate()` at line 133.
- Add a targeted integration test in `tests/test_finalize_acquisition.py` that calls `run_finalize` end-to-end and asserts the key is present with the correct `aspect_match` value.
- Audit whether `acquisition_provenance.source` is written anywhere in the acquisition workflow; document the gap if not.

## Non-Goals

- Do not wire `attribution_match` or `link_alive` into `source_quality_inputs` — those come from source-side metadata not yet connected to `finalize_acquisition.py`; stub them as `None`.
- Do not change `source_quality.py::extract_signals()` — the reader is correct; only the writer needs to change.
- Do not backfill existing sidecars in `samples/` — this is a forward-only fix for new acquisitions.
- Do not change the sidecar JSON schema — `meta['verification'].additionalProperties` is already `true`, so the new key passes validation without a schema update.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a test that adds `source_quality_inputs` to the sidecar but does not assert the `aspect_match` value (e.g. only checks the key exists with `in meta["verification"]`) is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break criterion must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `src/fine_art_archive/collect/verify.py`, add `VerificationReport.to_source_quality_inputs(self) -> dict` after `to_dict()` at line 63. Iterate `self.checks`; for the check named `"aspect_ratio"`, map `status=="PASS"` → `True`, `"FAIL"` → `False`, `"SKIP"` or absent → `None`. For `"perceptual_hash"`, map the same way to `phash_match`. Return `{"phash_match": ..., "aspect_match": ..., "dim_match": None}` (dim_match is always `None` until a dimension-check layer is wired).
- [ ] In `scripts/finalize_acquisition.py`, after the closing brace of `meta["verification"]` at line 105, add: `meta["verification"]["source_quality_inputs"] = vreport.to_source_quality_inputs()`. This line must appear before `sidecar.validate(meta)` at line 133.
- [ ] In `tests/test_finalize_acquisition.py`, add test `test_run_finalize_writes_source_quality_inputs(tmp_path)`: create a landscape JPEG using the existing `_make_jpeg(tmp_path / "master.jpg", w=400, h=300)`, write a minimal `meta.json` with `dimensions_original: {h_cm: 30.0, w_cm: 40.0}`, the required `files.master` scaffold, and an empty `history` list, call `fa.run_finalize(tmp_path, refetch_master_hash=True)`, and assert `meta["verification"]["source_quality_inputs"]["aspect_match"] is True` (400×300 px aspect 1.333 matches 40cm×30cm aspect 1.333 within threshold).
- [ ] In the same test, assert `meta["verification"]["source_quality_inputs"]["phash_match"] is None` (no reference image supplied, so the perceptual-hash check was skipped).
- [ ] Run `rg 'acquisition_provenance' scripts/ src/` to confirm whether any script writes `acquisition_provenance.source`. If no writer exists (current grep: only `source_quality.py:305` reads it), add a `# TODO: set acquisition_provenance.source on museum-API acquisitions` comment at `finalize_acquisition.py::run_finalize()` near the provenance block so the gap is visible when museum API flow is wired.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_finalize_acquisition.py::test_run_finalize_writes_source_quality_inputs` passes: the returned `meta` has `verification["source_quality_inputs"]` with keys `phash_match`, `aspect_match`, `dim_match`; `aspect_match` is `True` for the landscape fixture (400×300 px, 40cm×30cm).
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate**: temporarily remove the line `meta["verification"]["source_quality_inputs"] = vreport.to_source_quality_inputs()` from `finalize_acquisition.py`. The named test above must FAIL with a `KeyError` on `source_quality_inputs`. Restore the line; test passes. Capture the failure output in the PR.
- [ ] `rg 'source_quality_inputs' src/ scripts/` returns at least two distinct file hits: the reader at `src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py:308` and the new writer at `scripts/finalize_acquisition.py` (line ~106).
- [ ] After re-running `scripts/finalize_acquisition.py samples/0441b1c-the-little-street-vermeer` (or any sample with known `h_cm`/`w_cm`), the updated `meta.json` contains `verification.source_quality_inputs` with a non-null `aspect_match` value.

## Implementation Notes

- `src/fine_art_archive/collect/verify.py:36-63` — `VerificationReport` dataclass; `to_dict()` is at line 51; add `to_source_quality_inputs()` immediately after.
- `src/fine_art_archive/collect/verify.py:66-116` — `check_aspect_ratio()`: returns `CheckResult(name="aspect_ratio", status=...)` with `status` in `{"PASS","FAIL","SKIP"}`.
- `src/fine_art_archive/collect/verify.py:119-174` — `check_perceptual_hash()`: returns `CheckResult(name="perceptual_hash", ...)`, only appended when both `candidate_path` and `reference_path` are supplied (`verify.py:201-209`).
- `scripts/finalize_acquisition.py:86-105` — `vreport = verify(...)` call and the `meta["verification"]` write block; new `source_quality_inputs` line goes immediately after line 105.
- `scripts/finalize_acquisition.py:133` — `sidecar.validate(meta)`; the new line must precede this call.
- `src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py:294-332` — `extract_signals()`: reads `v.get("source_quality_inputs") or {}` at line 308; sets `phash_match`, `aspect_match`, `dim_match` on the returned `SignalRow`.
- `src/fine_art_archive/quality/source_quality.py:77-103` — `SignalRow` dataclass; the fields the new writer must populate are `phash_match`, `aspect_match`, `dim_match` (all `bool | None`).
- `config/source_quality.yaml` — all 8 real sources show `n_acquired: 0`, `first_seen: null`, null empirical signals; confirms the real-source signal path is entirely dark until this fix lands.
- `tests/test_finalize_acquisition.py:23-27` — existing `_make_jpeg()` helper; reuse it for the landscape fixture.
- `tests/test_source_quality.py` — existing test surface for `extract_signals()`; a follow-on test there (after this fix) would close the round-trip, but that is not required for this issue.

body:
## Why

`POST /works/{work_id}/rate` (`src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:542-581`) is the sole intake path for the preference-model event log at `data/ratings_log.jsonl` (defined at `main.py:22`). The endpoint validates five separate conditions before writing — all-None payload (line 545), unknown `rating` value (line 547), unknown `surface` (line 549), unknown chip id from `selected_reasons` (line 553), and missing work (line 558) — then appends a JSON event that downstream Parquet rollups consume as training data. None of this code path is exercised under CI: `grep -n 'POST\|/rate\|subject_action' tests/test_companion_app_api.py` returns zero matches. `tests/test_companion_app_api.py:23-78` covers eight GET endpoints but stops at the read surface entirely. This is **latent fragility, not a current break**: the validation logic exists and is correct today, but a field rename in `RatingIn` (`main.py:478-532`), a range change in the `SURFACES` set (`main.py:449-475`), or a regression in the event-dict assembly (`lines 561-576`) could merge with a green test run.

## Scope

- Add a monkeypatch fixture in `tests/test_companion_app_api.py` that redirects `RATINGS_LOG` writes to a `tmp_path` file so CI does not touch the real `data/ratings_log.jsonl`.
- Add a happy-path POST test that exercises the full write path and asserts the returned event dict shape matches the JSONL spec.
- Add four targeted tests covering the main validation-failure paths (unknown surface, unknown chip id, all-None payload) and the 404 path for a missing work.
- Scope is strictly `POST /works/{work_id}/rate`.

## Non-Goals

- Do not add tests for `POST /subject_action` or `POST /variant_upgrades/{wid}/decision` — those endpoints have their own write paths and are out of scope.
- Do not add tests for the preference model or the Parquet rollup (issue #21 is BLOCKED).
- Do not test JSONL file persistence by reading the written file back from disk — an assertion on the returned event dict is the correct scope.
- Do not test the deprecated single-axis `rating` field beyond the all-None-payload guard; the two-axis `quality + fit` scheme is the forward path.
- Scaffold-only completion does NOT count: a test that POSTs to the endpoint but only asserts `status_code == 200` without asserting the event shape fields (`event_kind`, `quality`, `fit`, `scheme`, `selected_reasons`) is a failure of this issue. The deliberate-break criterion must be demonstrated.

## Tasks

- [ ] In `tests/test_companion_app_api.py`, add a `@pytest.fixture` that uses `monkeypatch` to set `fine_art_archive.api.main.RATINGS_LOG` to `tmp_path / "ratings_log.jsonl"` for the duration of each POST test. Also monkeypatch `fine_art_archive.api.store.get_work` to return a stub dict `{"work_id": work_id}` so the happy-path test bypasses the archive lookup (line 558) without loading real sample data.
- [ ] Add test `test_rate_work_write_path`: using the TestClient, POST `{"quality": 8, "fit": 6, "surface": "companion-app", "selected_reasons": ["affect:somber"]}` to `/works/test-wid/rate`, assert `status_code == 200`, and assert the response body has `event["event_kind"] == "rating"`, `event["quality"] == 8`, `event["fit"] == 6`, `event["scheme"] == "two-axis-10"`, `event["work_id"] == "test-wid"`, and `event["selected_reasons"] == ["affect:somber"]`.
- [ ] Add test `test_rate_work_unknown_surface`: POST `{"quality": 5, "surface": "not-a-valid-surface-xyz"}` to `/works/test-wid/rate`, assert `status_code == 400` (guard at `main.py:549`).
- [ ] Add test `test_rate_work_unknown_chip_id`: POST `{"quality": 5, "surface": "companion-app", "selected_reasons": ["not-a-real:chip"]}` to `/works/test-wid/rate`, assert `status_code == 400` (guard at `main.py:553`).
- [ ] Add test `test_rate_work_all_none_payload`: POST `{"quality": null, "fit": null, "rating": null, "surface": "companion-app"}` to `/works/test-wid/rate`, assert `status_code == 400` (guard at `main.py:545`).
- [ ] Add test `test_rate_missing_work_404`: without patching `store.get_work`, POST a valid two-axis rating to `/works/no-such-wid/rate`, assert `status_code == 404` (guard at `main.py:558`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pytest tests/test_companion_app_api.py::test_rate_work_write_path` passes: response is 200 and `response.json()["event"]["event_kind"] == "rating"`, `["quality"] == 8`, `["fit"] == 6`, `["scheme"] == "two-axis-10"`.
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_companion_app_api.py::test_rate_work_unknown_surface tests/test_companion_app_api.py::test_rate_work_unknown_chip_id tests/test_companion_app_api.py::test_rate_work_all_none_payload tests/test_companion_app_api.py::test_rate_missing_work_404` all pass.
- [ ] **Deliberate-break gate**: temporarily edit `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:549` to replace `if body.surface not in SURFACES:` with `if False:` (disabling the surface guard). `test_rate_work_unknown_surface` must FAIL with an assertion error (expected 400, got 200). Revert; test passes. Capture the failure output in the PR.
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_companion_app_api.py -q` collects and passes all 8 existing GET tests plus all 6 new tests with no regressions.
- [ ] The monkeypatch fixture prevents writes to the real `data/ratings_log.jsonl`: verified by asserting the patched `tmp_path / "ratings_log.jsonl"` is non-empty after `test_rate_work_write_path` (confirming the write went to the tmp file, not silently dropped).

## Implementation Notes

- `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:22` — `RATINGS_LOG = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "ratings_log.jsonl"`; patch this name in `fine_art_archive.api.main` via `monkeypatch.setattr`.
- `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:478-532` — `RatingIn` Pydantic model: `quality` and `fit` are `int | None` (1-10), `rating` is `int | None` (-2..+2), `surface` defaults to `"companion-app"`, `selected_reasons` is a `list[str]` of `"group:chip"` format, `scheme` defaults to `"two-axis-10"`.
- `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:449-475` — `SURFACES` set: `{"companion-app", "frame-tv-65", "frame-tv-55", "ipad", "sd-card-batch", "review"}`; use `"companion-app"` as the valid surface in tests.
- `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:542-581` — `rate_work()` function: validation guards at lines 545, 547, 549, 553, 558; event dict at lines 561-576; JSONL append at lines 577-579; `store.invalidate_ratings_cache()` at line 580.
- `src/fine_art_archive/api/store.py:118` — `get_work(work_id: str) -> dict | None`; monkeypatch to return a stub dict for the happy-path and 400 tests.
- `src/fine_art_archive/api/store.py:223-227` — `count_ratings_for(work_id)` is also called in the 200 response (`main.py:581`); the TestClient's in-memory store will return 0 for any unseen work_id, which is fine for the test.
- `tests/test_companion_app_api.py:18-20` — existing module-scoped `client` fixture (`TestClient(app)`); reuse for all new tests.
- `tests/test_companion_app_api.py:23-78` — the 8 existing GET tests; do not modify them.
- `src/fine_art_archive/api/main.py:8` — module docstring confirms `data/ratings_log.jsonl` append-only write contract and the JSONL schema compatibility with `preference_model_design.md` event spec.

body:
## Why

`display/hints.py` emits per-device render PARAMETERS — `build_display_hints` (`display/hints.py:61`) returns a dict with `dither`, `saturation_boost`, `contrast_boost`, and `gamut_target: "spectra6"` for the two E-Ink targets (`inkposter_tela_28_5` at `display/hints.py:88-93`, `pimoroni_inky_13_3` at `:94-99`). But **no code does the pixel work**: there is no dither kernel and no gamut quantization to the Spectra-6 palette anywhere in `src/` (grep for dither/gamut/spectra returns only these parameter strings + the `pick_dither` selector at `display/hints.py:52`). `NEXT_PHASE_PLAN` Phase D calls for the E-Ink render pipeline. Missing behavior: turning a master + its `display_hints` into a Spectra-6 palette image.

**Latent** — the feature is simply absent (no current break). Device delivery (push vs SD-card) is explicitly deferred (`NEXT_PHASE_PLAN` Phase D) and is out of scope.

## Scope

Add `src/fine_art_archive/display/render.py`: render a master to a device's native resolution, apply the named dither, and quantize to the fixed Spectra-6 6-color palette. Pillow + numpy only (both core deps). Produces the rendered FILE only — no device I/O.

## Non-Goals

Do NOT implement device delivery / SD-card / push APIs (deferred per `NEXT_PHASE_PLAN` Phase D).

Do NOT modify `display/hints.py` (it stays the parameter source).

Do NOT add the saliency / crop-safety score (needs a pretrained model — separate, gated).

**Scaffold-only does NOT count:** a `render_for_device` whose output contains colors outside the 6-color palette, or that is not at the device's native dimensions, fails this issue. The deliberate-break gate must be demonstrated.

# Wire source-quality scoring into acquisition routing

## Why
The source-quality scoring library is fully built and unit-tested but **not wired into acquisition** — routing ignores it. `quality/source_quality.py` computes per-(source, work_class) composite scores (`score_for`, `source_quality.py:225`; `composite_score`, `source_quality.py:216`) and is covered by `tests/test_source_quality.py` (11 tests, green). But `collect/acquisition_flow.py` does **not import it** (imports are `acquisition_flow.py:27-42`), and `run_acquisition_flow` selects by pure truncation — `selected = work_dirs[:max_items]` (`acquisition_flow.py:132`) — no scoring, no work-class, no candidate comparison. `score_for` has **zero call sites** outside tests.

Design commitment (`source_quality_design.md:78-88`): when multiple sources can supply a work, look up each candidate's composite score for that class; if top − 2nd ≥ 0.10 use the top, else try top first with fallback. Missing behavior: that score-based ordering does not exist.

**Latent fragility, not a current break** — scoring works in isolation; it is simply never consulted.

## Scope
Add score-based source ranking to `collect/acquisition_flow.py`, consuming the existing `source_quality.score_for`. Additive: existing single-source `run_acquisition_flow` behavior is preserved.

## Non-Goals
- Do NOT modify the scoring math in `quality/source_quality.py` (`composite_score`/`blended_stats`/`verify_pass`) — source of truth, already tested.
- Do NOT build the nightly aggregator or the link-health probe (separate issues).
- Do NOT accept scaffold-only implementations: a `rank_sources()` never called by `run_acquisition_flow`, or a test that does not exercise the ≥0.10 margin rule, is a failure of this issue.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add `from fine_art_archive.quality import source_quality` to `collect/acquisition_flow.py` (imports currently at `acquisition_flow.py:27-42`)
- [ ] Create the `rank_sources(work_class: str, candidate_sources: list[str], aggregates: dict) -> list[tuple[str, float]]` function signature with type hints in `collect/acquisition_flow.py`
- [ ] Implement the loop in `rank_sources` that calls `source_quality.score_for(src, work_class, aggregates=aggregates)` for each candidate source with the provided aggregates
- [ ] Add the sorting logic to `rank_sources` to return sources ordered by score descending as tuples of source name and score
- [ ] Create the `select_source(work_class: str, candidate_sources: list[str], aggregates: dict) -> tuple[str, str]` function signature with type hints in `collect/acquisition_flow.py`
- [ ] Implement the margin calculation logic in `select_source` to compare the top two ranked sources using a 0.10 threshold
- [ ] Add the conditional return logic to `select_source` that returns the chosen source with reason `"margin"` or `"tied-fallback"` based on the threshold
- [ ] Add the optional `candidate_sources` parameter with type hint `list[str] | None = None` to the `run_acquisition_flow` function signature (around `acquisition_flow.py:114`)
- [ ] Implement conditional logic in `run_acquisition_flow` to call `select_source` when `candidate_sources` is provided and extract the chosen source
- [ ] Verify that existing behavior in `run_acquisition_flow` is preserved by maintaining the current code path when `candidate_sources` is None
- [ ] Create the test file `tests/test_acquisition_routing.py` with necessary imports and fixture setup for synthetic aggregates
- [ ] Implement `test_rank_sources_orders_by_score` in `tests/test_acquisition_routing.py` to verify sources are ordered by descending composite score
- [ ] Implement `test_select_source_margin_rule` in `tests/test_acquisition_routing.py` to verify both margin and tied-fallback scenarios with different score gaps

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `tests/test_acquisition_routing.py::test_rank_sources_orders_by_score` passes: with a synthetic `aggregates` where `"rijksmuseum"` composite_score is 0.90 and `"met"` is 0.70 for work_class `"western-painting-19c"`, `rank_sources(...)` returns `"rijksmuseum"` before `"met"`
- [ ] The test `test_rank_sources_orders_by_score` asserts that the first returned source is `"rijksmuseum"` when rijksmuseum has score 0.90 and met has score 0.70
- [ ] A comment exists in `test_rank_sources_orders_by_score` documenting that reversing the sort order in `rank_sources` will cause the assertion to fail, demonstrating the test validates sort direction
- [ ] `tests/test_acquisition_routing.py::test_select_source_margin_rule` passes: 0.90 vs 0.70 returns `("rijksmuseum","margin")`; 0.90 vs 0.85 returns the top source with reason `"tied-fallback"`
- [ ] Regression anchor passes: `tests/test_source_quality.py::test_verify_pass_all_gates_required` (`tests/test_source_quality.py:48`, assertion at line 66) still passes
- [ ] `pr-00-gate` is green

## Implementation Notes
`score_for(source, work_class, *, aggregates)` is at `quality/source_quality.py:225`; unknown source → tier-1 prior, `n_acquired=0` (`source_quality.py:233`). Tests can pass a hand-built `aggregates` dict — no YAML, no network, no images.

Confirmed-green local repro before changes (repo root, after `pip install -e ".[dev]"`): `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_source_quality.py tests/test_acquisition_flow.py -q` → passes.

The ≥0.10 margin rule is specified in `source_quality_design.md:84-88`: when multiple sources can supply a work, look up each candidate's composite score for that class; if top − 2nd ≥ 0.10 use the top, else try top first with fallback.

## Deferred Tasks (Requires Human)
- [ ] Run the deliberate-break verification: temporarily reverse the sort order in `rank_sources(...)` (ascending), run `pytest` to confirm `tests/test_acquisition_routing.py::test_rank_sources_orders_by_score` fails (returns `"met"` first), then revert the sort and confirm the test passes again

## Why
New acquisitions must be dedup-checked against the archive **before** promotion — replacing the name+size guessing that the 2026-05-25 batch showed was wrong (DECISIONS **D017**). The cascade pieces now all live in-repo (after #2/#3/#4): `collect/dedupe.py`, `collect/acquisition_flow.py`, and the `scripts/perceptual_dedupe.py` / `scripts/visual_dedupe.py` tools.

## Scope
Add a promotion gate to the acquire path (`collect/acquisition_flow.py`) that runs the cheapest-first cascade and returns a verdict per candidate:
1. **sha256** — exact byte match against the archive.
2. **pHash (dHash+aHash, dHam ≤ 13)** — near-identical reproductions, via the archive pHash cache.
3. **artist-Q-ID block** — narrow candidates to the same creator Q-ID.
4. **metadata narrow** — genre/depicts/date within the artist.
5. **DINOv2** — vision confirmation on the small residual (pluggable hook; operational).

## Tasks
- [ ] Add `dedup_check(candidate) -> Verdict{new | duplicate_of:<wid> | needs_review}` wiring layers 1–4 (torch-free) against the archive pHash cache.
- [ ] Wire it into `run_acquisition_flow` so a candidate is gated before promotion.
- [ ] Expose the DINOv2 layer (scripts/visual_dedupe.py) as an injectable hook — default off in-repo, run operationally in the `.faa-venv`.
- [ ] Tests for layers 1–4 on synthetic data (identical → duplicate; unrelated → new).

## Acceptance
- [ ] `run_acquisition_flow` emits a promotion verdict per candidate.
- [ ] A candidate identical to an archived work is flagged `duplicate_of` via sha256/pHash.
- [ ] Cheap layers covered by CI tests; DINOv2 layer documented as operational.
- [ ] `pr-00-gate` green.

## Notes
- Cheap layers (sha256/pHash/Q-ID/metadata) are torch-free and CI-testable; the DINOv2 residual stays operational (needs torch + the archive embed cache, which live in Cowork).
- The archive pHash cache (`archive_phash_cache.json`) and DINOv2 embeds live in the Cowork workspace; the in-repo code should take the cache path as input so tests use a synthetic cache.
- Companion Phase-B work that stays in **Cowork** (not this repo): the work-Q-ID + Wikidata metadata backfill, and the G18 promotion of the validated 29-work batch into `Art/works/`.

## Why
Bring the importable domain library into this repo so the Gate runs against it.

## Scope
Copy the following from the local Claude Project workspace (Dropbox/Pictures/Claude Project; see `consumer_repo_handoff/MANIFEST.md` for the exact files + `EXCLUDES`):
- `src/fine_art_archive/` (sidecar, parsers, collect, display)

- `tests/`

Remove the template placeholder `src/my_project` and keep the `pyproject` name `fine-art-archive`.

## Non-Goals
- Renaming the package from `fine-art-archive` to another name
- Modifying the copied source code beyond applying EXCLUDES rules
- Setting up new test infrastructure (use existing tests as-is)

## Tasks
- [ ] Remove the template placeholder directory `src/my_project`

> ⚠️ **BLOCKER**: The following tasks require access to local filesystem paths (Dropbox/Pictures/Claude Project) that remote agents cannot access. These tasks must be completed by:
